## 1.3 Scope

**In scope:** the 18 planned areas of the BRD, the login page, the shared application shell (header, navigation, filters, info and Expand analysis components), the two API routes, the CSV dataset and its validation, the synthetic data generator as the source of every value, the KPI layer, the scenario engine, authentication, and the automated tests.

**Out of scope:** changes to the application (this is a documentation-only task); production identity, live integrations, real company data, deployment to GitHub or Vercel (not configured), and any statistical or machine-learning forecasting (none exists).

## 1.5 Assumptions, limitations and unresolved decisions

- All values quoted are for the default filters (Year to date 2026-01 to 2026-09, USD, all business units) unless stated, and come from the committed dataset (seed 20261029, dataset version 2026.10.1, cut-off 2026-09-30).
- The BRD is a draft. Where this document says "Implemented", it describes what the code does, **not** that the behaviour has been approved.
- The data model .docx named in the request was not available (CNF-10).
- The application folder is not a Git repository; no Vercel deployment exists.
- Charts could not be inspected visually in a browser for this document; chart descriptions come from the chart option code.
- Conflicts between sources are recorded in Section 17 (CNF-01…10), not silently resolved. Open decisions are DEC-01…12; recommended defaults are proposals only.

# 2. Product Overview

## 2.1 What BLS OneView is

BLS OneView is an **interview demonstration** of an enterprise business-intelligence and analytics web application for a language services provider. It brings commercial, translation, interpretation, quality, workforce, capacity, finance, AI, technology, risk, forecasting and governance information into one navigable application with 18 tabs. It runs on Next.js 16 (App Router, server components) with Apache ECharts, and reads a synthetic, validated CSV dataset produced offline by a deterministic Python generator.

## 2.2 Business problem

The BRD (SRC-01, section 2.2) describes the problems the prototype illustrates:

- **Fragmented visibility** — commercial, production, dispatch, quality and finance data live in separate systems.
- **Margin pressure** — leaders need service-line profitability, vendor cost and the effect of AI-assisted workflows.
- **Capacity constraints** — demand can exceed qualified linguists for some languages and weeks.
- **Service risk** — late projects, unfilled requests, quality disputes and client-health issues need early attention.
- **Reactive decisions** — operational drivers are rarely connected to revenue, margin, retention and scenarios.

## 2.3 Intended users and decisions

| Persona | Responsibilities | Decisions supported | Main screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executive (CEO/COO/CFO) | Overall performance, plan, risk | Are we on plan? Which area explains a variance? Which risks need action? | Overview, Executive Strategy, Risk & Alerts, Forecasting & Scenarios |
| Sales and account leader | Pipeline, accounts, retention | Which accounts and deals matter? Where does the funnel leak? | Client & Revenue, Sales & Marketing |
| Translation operations leader | Written production and SLAs | Which batches and pairs are late? How much work is AI-touched? | Translation Ops, AI & Automation |
| Interpretation operations leader | OPI, VRI, on-site service levels | Are calls answered and requests filled? | Interpretation Ops |
| Quality and vendor manager | LQA, disputes, corrective actions | Where do errors cluster? Which actions are open? | Quality & Compliance, HR & Workforce |
| Workforce / capacity planner | Linguist supply, PM workload | Which pairs will be short? Are PMs overloaded? | Capacity & Demand, HR & Workforce |
| Finance analyst | P&L, margins, receivables | Where is margin earned? Who owes money? | Finance & Profitability |
| Data steward / architect | Data quality, lineage, integrations | Can the data be trusted? Which simulated connectors are degraded? | Data Governance, Technology & Integration |
| Interview reviewer | Evaluates product and data thinking | Is the reasoning sound and transparent? | All, especially info icons and Data Governance |

## 2.4 Expected business value (illustrative)

One consistent filter context and one KPI layer (`core()`) mean the same revenue appears on Overview, Client & Revenue and Finance; every metric carries its definition, formula, source and caveats; and the "fail-closed" data loader prevents numbers from being calculated on invalid data. Because the data is synthetic, the value shown is the **method**, not any business result.

## 2.5 Navigation and information architecture

The sidebar groups the 18 tabs into three groups (the BRD suggested other cluster names; the implemented grouping follows the BRD priority framework):

| Group (sidebar label) | Tabs in order |
|---|---|
| Core tabs | Overview · Executive Strategy · Client & Revenue · Translation Ops · Interpretation Ops · Finance & Profitability · AI & Automation · Forecasting & Scenarios |
| Secondary tabs | Sales & Marketing · Quality & Compliance · HR & Workforce · Capacity & Demand · Technology & Integration · Risk & Alerts · Data Governance |
| Concept tabs | Enhancement · Coming Soon · Feedback |

`/` redirects to `/overview`; `/login` is the only public page. Every dashboard tab uses the same shell: header (logo, title, DEMO badge, global filters, Sign out), sidebar (or mobile drawer) and a scrolling main area. Global filters live in the URL (`range`, `from`, `to`, `cur`, `bu`), so views can be bookmarked and shared; the sidebar keeps them when switching tab.

## 2.6 Kinds of analytics in the application

| Kind | Question | Where it appears | What it is in this app |
|---|---|---|---|
| Descriptive | What happened? | KPI cards, trend charts, tables on every data tab | Aggregations of synthetic facts for the selected months |
| Diagnostic | Why did it happen? | Expand analysis: prior-period change, target vs actual, breakdowns, drill-down, largest movers, generated insight text | Same formulas applied to segments |
| Predictive | What will happen? | Capacity forecast weeks; revenue trajectory ranges | **Not a statistical prediction.** Forecast weeks are generated by the data generator (recent average × seasonality × growth × noise + a seeded surge); trajectories apply fixed growth rates. No model is trained or evaluated. |
| Scenario | What if we change X? | Forecasting & Scenarios | Transparent formula SCN-F1.0 applied to the trailing-12-month baseline |

## 2.7 Interview prototype versus production solution

| Aspect | This prototype | A production solution would need |
|---|---|---|
| Data | Synthetic CSV, fixed seed, validated on load | Governed warehouse fed by TMS, telephony, CRM, ERP/finance and HR systems |
| Identity | One shared username/password, signed cookie, no rate limit | SSO, MFA, role-based access, audit trail |
| Persistence | Votes, acknowledgements, feedback and scenarios are browser-only | Durable storage with ownership and history |
| Forecasting | Fixed formulas and generated forecast weeks | Statistical or ML models with back-testing and intervals |
| Integrations | Simulated telemetry on `.invalid` endpoints | Real monitoring |
| Operations | Single process cache; not deployed | Hosting, monitoring, backups, SLAs |

<!-- pagebreak -->
# 4. Detailed Screen-by-Screen Functional Specification

Each subsection answers eleven questions. Calculations and sources are summarised per component; the full attribute set of every KPI is in Section 5 and of every chart and table in Section 6. Values are for the default filters (Year to date, USD, all units).

## 4.1 SCR-01 Overview

### 1. Why the screen exists
Leaders otherwise read revenue, delivery, quality and finance figures from different systems with different filters. Objective: Enterprise pulse: one-screen health check across revenue, profit, delivery, AI and risk.

### 2. Who uses it
Executives (CEO/COO/CFO); operations directors; interview reviewer.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Page header 'Overview' with subtitle and period chip
2. Row 1: ten KPI cards KPI-OV-001…010 (5 per row on wide screens)
3. Row 2: CH-OV-001 (left), CH-OV-002 (right)
4. Row 3: TB-OV-001
5. Footer note on synthetic data and currency

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-OV-001 Revenue | Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. Not bookings, invoices or cash. | $1.07M (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-002 Gross margin | Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. | 42.1% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-003 EBITDA margin | EBITDA / recognised revenue. | 14.8% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-004 Active clients | Clients with recognised revenue > 0 in the selected range. | 53 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-005 Net revenue retention (TTM) | Fixed opening cohort = clients with revenue in the 12 months ending 12 months before the range end. NRR = cohort revenue in the latest 12 months / cohort revenue in the opening 12 months. New clients are excluded; expansion and contraction included. | 110.9% (Latest 12 months vs opening 12 months) |
| KPI-OV-006 Translation on-time delivery | Delivered batches with delivered_date <= due_date divided by all delivered batches in the range. | 93.8% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-007 OPI speed to answer | Mean seconds to connect for FULFILLED on-demand OPI sessions. Applies to OPI only. | 38 s (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-008 AI-touched word share | Words in AI-touched workflows (MTPE or AIR) divided by delivered written words in the same range and population as TR_WORDS. | 44.0% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-009 Quality score | Mean evaluation score on the single illustrative 0-100 framework (ILLUSTRATIVE_MQM_STYLE): 100 minus weighted error penalties per 1,000 sampled words (minor 1, major 5, critical 25). | 95.6 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-OV-010 DSO (days) | Simplified demo DSO: open receivables at the range end divided by invoiced value in the trailing 90 days, times 90. Receivable = invoiced less allocated cash receipts received on or before the range end. | 42.6 (Days, at 2026-09-30) |
| CH-OV-001 Revenue and EBITDA by month | How revenue and operating profit moved over 33 months, including seasonality. | - |
| CH-OV-002 Revenue by service line | Which service lines generate revenue in the period. | - |
| TB-OV-001 Open alerts (rule-derived, top 8 by severity) | What the most severe open risks are. | - |

Interpretation notes: Green/red change badges compare with the prior period in the favourable direction for each KPI. EBITDA with a unit selected is an allocation, not a unit P&L.

### 5. What decision it supports
Is the business on track this period, and which area needs a closer look?

- KPI-OV-001 Revenue: Decide whether growth is on track and which segment explains a change (via Expand analysis).
- KPI-OV-002 Gross margin: Identify margin erosion by service line or tier.
- KPI-OV-003 EBITDA margin: Judge whether growth converts into operating profit.
- KPI-OV-004 Active clients: Spot shrinking or growing client counts.
- KPI-OV-005 Net revenue retention (TTM): Prioritise retention and expansion actions.
- KPI-OV-006 Translation on-time delivery: Find language pairs or workflows causing late delivery.
- KPI-OV-007 OPI speed to answer: Adjust interpreter staffing for slow languages or hours.
- KPI-OV-008 AI-touched word share: Track AI adoption against strategy.
- KPI-OV-009 Quality score: Target quality interventions.
- KPI-OV-010 DSO (days): Trigger collections follow-up.

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-OV-001, KPI-OV-004, CH-OV-002 | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client for business unit) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id, service_line_id, unit_type, units; dim_client.business_unit | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-OV-002, KPI-OV-003, CH-OV-001 | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-OV-005 | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.client_id, month_id, revenue_usd; dim_client.business_unit | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-OV-006, KPI-OV-008 | fact_translation_batch (+ fact_project for client, dim_client for unit) | fact_translation_batch.status, delivered_date, due_date, start_date, words_total, tm_match_words, workflow_id, client_rejected, project_id; fact_project.client_id | public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-OV-007 | fact_interpretation_session (+ dim_client) | fact_interpretation_session.request_date, status, service_line_id, request_type, duration_min, connect_seconds, client_id | public/data/fact_interpretation_session.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-OV-009 | fact_quality_evaluation (+ fact_translation_batch → fact_project for client) | fact_quality_evaluation.eval_date, score, outcome, dispute_status, corrective_action, corrective_status, critical_count, major_count, minor_count, sample_words, batch_id | public/data/fact_quality_evaluation.csv, public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv |
| KPI-OV-010 | fact_invoice_line, bridge_payment_invoice, fact_payment (+ dim_client) | fact_invoice_line.invoice_line_id, client_id, invoice_date, due_date, amount_usd; bridge_payment_invoice.allocated_usd, payment_id, invoice_line_id; fact_payment.payment_date | public/data/fact_invoice_line.csv, public/data/bridge_payment_invoice.csv, public/data/fact_payment.csv |
| TB-OV-001 | fact_risk_alert | fact_risk_alert.status, severity, domain, exposure_usd, likelihood, impact, rule_id | public/data/fact_risk_alert.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-OV-001 | REV = Σ fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd for lines with month_id in the selected months and client in the selected unit; displayed = REV ÷ fx(cur) | Recognition month (fact_revenue_line.month_id); Selected reporting period (whole months) | Applied through dim_client.business_unit | Converted once from the USD total: value ÷ dim_fx_rate.usd_per_unit |
| KPI-OV-002 | GM = (REV − DIRECT) ÷ REV, where DIRECT = Σ fact_cost_line.amount_usd with cost_class = DIRECT attached (revenue_id) to the in-scope revenue lines | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-OV-003 | EBITDA_M = (GP − OPEX_alloc) ÷ REV; OPEX_alloc = Σ OPEX of the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV) | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-OV-004 | COUNT DISTINCT client_id whose Σ revenue_usd in the selected months > 0 | Recognition month (fact_revenue_line.month_id); Selected reporting period (whole months) | Applied through dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-OV-005 | Cohort = clients with revenue > 0 in 2024-10..2025-09; NRR = Σ cohort revenue 2025-10..2026-09 ÷ Σ cohort revenue 2024-10..2025-09 | Fixed windows: opening 2024-10..2025-09, latest 2025-10..2026-09; Not applied: fixed at the 2026-09-30 cut-off | Applied (narrows the cohort) | Ratio: not affected |
| KPI-OV-006 | TR_OTD = COUNT(delivered batches with delivered_date ≤ due_date) ÷ COUNT(delivered batches), delivered in the selected months | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-OV-007 | OPI_ASA = mean(connect_seconds) over sessions with service_line_id = OPI, request_type = ON_DEMAND, status = FULFILLED | Request month (month of request_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via client_id | Not applicable |
| KPI-OV-008 | AI_SHARE = Σ words_total (workflow_id ≠ HT) ÷ Σ words_total, delivered batches in the selected months | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-OV-009 | QUALITY_SCORE = mean(fact_quality_evaluation.score) for evaluations in the selected months; score = max(0, 100 − (minor×1 + major×5 + critical×25) × 1000 ÷ sample_words) | Evaluation month (month of eval_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via the evaluated batch's client | Not applicable |
| KPI-OV-010 | DSO = Σ open_usd ÷ Σ amount_usd of invoices dated 2026-07-03..2026-09-30 (last 90 days) × 90; open_usd = amount_usd − Σ allocations paid on or before 2026-09-30 | As at 2026-09-30 (invoice_date and payment_date ≤ cut-off); Not applied: fixed at the cut-off | Applied via client_id | Money converted once from USD totals |
| CH-OV-001 | monthlySeries(bu): per month Σ revenue_usd and Σ direct cost of in-scope lines; OPEX(month) × unit revenue share; EBITDA = revenue − direct − OPEX; values ÷ fx, rounded to whole units | Recognition month (month_id); All 33 months regardless of range; BU applies | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| CH-OV-002 | revBy(months, bu, service_line_id) sums revenue_usd; sorted descending; ÷ fx | Recognition month (fact_revenue_line.month_id); Selected reporting period (whole months) | Applied through dim_client.business_unit | Converted once from the USD total: value ÷ dim_fx_rate.usd_per_unit |
| TB-OV-001 | First 8 rows of fact_risk_alert with status ≠ RESOLVED, in file order (the generator sorts by severity, then exposure descending) | Snapshot at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied: always USD |

## 4.2 SCR-02 Executive Strategy

### 1. Why the screen exists
Plan, OKR and KPI-target information is usually held in slides and spreadsheets separate from actuals. Objective: Strategic plan tracking: revenue against plan, margins, and OKR progress.

### 2. Who uses it
Executives; strategy office.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header 'Executive Strategy' + period chip
2. Row 1: KPI-EX-001…004
3. Row 2: CH-EX-001 (left), CH-EX-002 (right)
4. Row 3: TB-EX-001 KPI scorecard
5. Row 4: TB-EX-002 OKR table
6. Badges 'Illustrative targets', 'Synthetic data'; note on OKR units

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-EX-001 Revenue vs plan | Whether revenue is ahead of or behind the illustrative plan. | 98.6% (YTD: $1.07M actual ÷ $1.09M plan) |
| KPI-EX-002 Gross margin | Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. | 42.1% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-EX-003 EBITDA | Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation = gross profit less operating expenses. D&A is shown separately below EBITDA in the bridge; interest and tax are out of scope. | $159.2K (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-EX-004 OKRs on track or complete | Share of strategic key results that are healthy. | 57% (8 of 14) |
| KPI-EX-005 OKR progress by pillar | Mean progress of key results, each capped at 100%. Progress = (current - baseline) / (target - baseline), with direction handled for lower-is-better metrics. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| KPI-EX-006 Scorecard attainment (6 KPIs) | One table of headline KPIs vs illustrative targets. | YTD: Revenue 98.6% (Near), GM 105.3% (On target), EBITDA margin 114.2% (On target), OTD 98.8% (Near), On-demand fill 101.0% (On target), Quality 103.9% (On target) |
| KPI-EX-007 Monthly revenue plan | Context for the plan line. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| CH-EX-001 Monthly revenue: actual vs plan | Is revenue tracking the illustrative plan month by month? | - |
| CH-EX-002 OKR progress by pillar | Which strategic pillar is furthest from its targets? | - |
| TB-EX-001 KPI scorecard | Which headline KPIs are on target? | - |
| TB-EX-002 Objectives and key results (as of the data cut-off) | Status of every key result. | - |

Interpretation notes: Plan is generated from actuals (rolling mean × 1.03), so it is illustrative and small gaps are expected. OKR progress is capped at 0–100%.

### 5. What decision it supports
Are we ahead of plan, and which strategic pillar is lagging?

- KPI-EX-001 Revenue vs plan: Escalate a plan shortfall.
- KPI-EX-002 Gross margin: As KPI-OV-002.
- KPI-EX-003 EBITDA: Assess operating leverage.
- KPI-EX-004 OKRs on track or complete: Focus leadership attention on at-risk pillars.
- KPI-EX-005 OKR progress by pillar: Re-plan the weakest pillar.
- KPI-EX-006 Scorecard attainment (6 KPIs): See which KPI is behind plan.
- KPI-EX-007 Monthly revenue plan: See when the plan was missed.

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-EX-001, KPI-EX-006, KPI-EX-007, CH-EX-001, TB-EX-001 | fact_revenue_line, fact_kpi_target_period | fact_kpi_target_period.kpi_id, month_id, target_value; fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd | public/data/fact_kpi_target_period.csv, public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv |
| KPI-EX-002, KPI-EX-003 | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| KPI-EX-004, KPI-EX-005, CH-EX-002, TB-EX-002 | fact_okr | fact_okr.status, progress, pillar, baseline_value, current_value, target_value | public/data/fact_okr.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-EX-001 | Attainment = REV ÷ PLAN; PLAN = Σ fact_kpi_target_period.target_value (kpi_id = REV) over the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV when a unit is selected) | Recognition month; Selected reporting period | Applied; the company plan is scaled by the unit's revenue share | Ratio: not affected |
| KPI-EX-002 | Same as KPI-OV-002 | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-EX-003 | EBITDA = GP − OPEX_alloc (see KPI-OV-003); displayed ÷ fx(cur) | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-EX-004 | COUNT(fact_okr.status ∈ {ON_TRACK, COMPLETE}) ÷ COUNT(fact_okr) | As at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied (money key results are USD) |
| KPI-EX-005 | mean(fact_okr.progress) per pillar; progress = clamp((current − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline), 0, 1) | As at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied (money key results are USD) |
| KPI-EX-006 | Attainment = actual ÷ target; REV target = Σ monthly plan (scaled by unit share); GM, EBITDA_M, TR_OTD, FILL_ON_DEMAND, QUALITY_SCORE targets = mean of monthly targets. Status: On target ≥ 100%, Near ≥ 97%, else Behind | Recognition month; Selected reporting period | Applied; the company plan is scaled by the unit's revenue share | Ratio: not affected |
| KPI-EX-007 | Plan(m) = fact_kpi_target_period.target_value (REV, month m) × (unit share of revenue over the selected period); generated as a centred 5-month rolling mean of actual revenue × 1.03 | Recognition month; All 33 months shown; the unit share uses the selected period | Applied; the company plan is scaled by the unit's revenue share | Ratio: not affected |
| CH-EX-001 | Actual from monthlySeries(bu); Plan = target_value(REV, month) × unit share of revenue over the selected period; ÷ fx | Recognition month; All 33 months; unit share uses the selected period | Applied; the company plan is scaled by the unit's revenue share | Ratio: not affected |
| CH-EX-002 | mean(progress) per pillar | As at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied (money key results are USD) |
| TB-EX-001 | Six KPIs from core(): REV, GM, EBITDA_M, TR_OTD, FILL_ON_DEMAND, QUALITY_SCORE vs fact_kpi_target_period | Recognition month; Selected reporting period | Applied; the company plan is scaled by the unit's revenue share | Ratio: not affected |
| TB-EX-002 | fact_okr joined to dim_owner.owner_code | As at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied (money key results are USD) |

### 8. How it behaves
Filters: Range, currency and business unit all apply (except where a component says otherwise). OKRs ignore range and unit (cut-off values). The monthly chart shows all 33 months. Interactions: Cards show no prior comparison on this tab. Scorecard has no expand analysis key.

Expand analysis keys: KPI-EX-001 → analysis `REV`, KPI-EX-002 → analysis `GM`, KPI-EX-003 → analysis `EBITDA`, KPI-EX-004 → analysis `ex.okr`, KPI-EX-005 → analysis `ex.okr`, KPI-EX-007 → analysis `REV`, CH-EX-001 → analysis `REV`, CH-EX-002 → analysis `ex.okr`, TB-EX-002 → analysis `ex.okr`. Expand without further analysis: TB-EX-001.
Info icons: every listed component has one (texts in Appendix L). Tooltips on charts: see Section 6. Tables: search, sort, paging and CSV export (IE-G-18…22) unless stated.

### 9. How to validate it
| Component | Validation / reconciliation |
|---|---|
| KPI-EX-001 | Recompute from fact_kpi_target_period; the Expand analysis 'Attainment' stat for REV shows the same value. |

| KPI-EX-003 | Parity test: matches data/generated/kpi_reference.json (independent pandas) within 1e-9 relative (tests/parity.test.ts). |

| TB-EX-002 | 14 rows. |

Screen acceptance: (1) Revenue vs plan = REV ÷ plan for the selected months. (2) Scorecard statuses follow On target ≥ 100%, Near ≥ 97%, else Behind. (3) OKR on-track share = 8/14 for the current dataset.

### 10. What happens when data is missing or invalid
No target for a month → that month is excluded from the plan sum; attainment n/a when the target is 0. Loading: skeleton (IE-G-27). Invalid dataset: 'Dataset unavailable' list (IE-G-28). Unexpected error: error boundary with 'Try again' (IE-G-26). Null ratios show 'n/a'; tables show 'No rows match the current filters.'; charts have no empty-state message (GAP-05).

### 11. Implementation status and outstanding gaps
Partially implemented (treemap, radar, EBITDA bridge and multi-year trajectory not built — GAP-15). Related register entries: GAP-11, GAP-15, CNF-02.

## 4.3 SCR-03 Client & Revenue

### 1. Why the screen exists
Concentration and churn risk are hard to see from invoice lists. Objective: Account performance, revenue concentration, retention and client health.

### 2. Who uses it
Sales and account leaders; executives.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header + period chip
2. Row 1: KPI-CR-001…005
3. Row 2: CH-CR-001, CH-CR-002, CH-CR-003
4. Row 3: CH-CR-004 (left), PN-CR-001 (right)
5. Row 4: TB-CR-001 client roster
6. Footer note

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-CR-001 Revenue | Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. Not bookings, invoices or cash. | $1.07M (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-CR-002 Active clients | Clients with recognised revenue > 0 in the selected range. | 53 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-CR-003 Revenue per active client | Revenue divided by active clients in the same range. | $20.2K (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-CR-004 Top-10 concentration | Share of revenue from the ten largest clients in the range. | 54.8% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-CR-005 Net revenue retention | Fixed opening cohort = clients with revenue in the 12 months ending 12 months before the range end. NRR = cohort revenue in the latest 12 months / cohort revenue in the opening 12 months. New clients are excluded; expansion and contraction included. | 110.9% (Latest 12 months vs opening 12 months) |
| KPI-CR-006 Gross revenue churn | Revenue-based gross churn for the NRR cohort: revenue lost from churn and contraction, ignoring expansion. | 13.1% (cohort of 56 clients) |
| KPI-CR-007 Logo retention | 1 - logo churn over the same cohort and window. | 92.9% |
| KPI-CR-008 Cohort size | Denominator of the retention measures. | 56 clients |
| KPI-CR-009 Client health score and band | Composite 0..1: 0.30 OTD(90d) + 0.25 quality(norm) + 0.20 payment timeliness + 0.25 revenue trend (weights renormalised for missing components). Bands: healthy >= 0.70, watch >= 0.50, else at risk. | 0.62 (Mean health score, 2026-09 snapshot) |
| CH-CR-001 Top 10 clients by revenue | Which clients matter most? | - |
| CH-CR-002 Revenue by tier | How revenue splits across Strategic, Growth and Standard tiers. | - |
| CH-CR-003 Revenue by vertical | Which industries drive revenue. | - |
| CH-CR-004 Client health bands (latest quarter-end) | How many clients are healthy, on watch or at risk. | - |
| PN-CR-001 Retention detail | How much revenue and how many clients the cohort retained. | - |
| TB-CR-001 Client roster | Profile of every client in scope. | - |

Interpretation notes: Top-10 concentration rising is unfavourable. Health score combines on-time delivery, quality, payment timeliness and revenue trend.

### 5. What decision it supports
Which accounts drive revenue, how concentrated is it, and which clients are at risk?

- KPI-CR-001 Revenue: As KPI-OV-001.
- KPI-CR-002 Active clients: As KPI-OV-004.
- KPI-CR-003 Revenue per active client: Pricing and account-growth focus.
- KPI-CR-004 Top-10 concentration: Diversification and key-account risk planning.
- KPI-CR-005 Net revenue retention: As KPI-OV-005.
- KPI-CR-006 Gross revenue churn: Size the retention problem.
- KPI-CR-007 Logo retention: Count-based retention view.
- KPI-CR-008 Cohort size: Judge how robust the retention figures are.
- KPI-CR-009 Client health score and band: Assign service-recovery actions.

| CH-CR-003 | Σ bars = KPI-CR-001. |
| CH-CR-004 | Counts sum to the number of clients with a 2026-09 snapshot. |
| PN-CR-001 | Matches the NRR analysis stats. |
| TB-CR-001 | Σ Revenue column = KPI-CR-001 when no tier/health filter is set. |

Screen acceptance: (1) Five KPI cards; NRR equals Overview. (2) Roster revenue sums to the Revenue card when no roster filter is set. (3) No real client names (fictional generator names).

### 10. What happens when data is missing or invalid
Clients without a 2026-09 snapshot show health '–' and band 'n/a'. Loading: skeleton (IE-G-27). Invalid dataset: 'Dataset unavailable' list (IE-G-28). Unexpected error: error boundary with 'Try again' (IE-G-26). Null ratios show 'n/a'; tables show 'No rows match the current filters.'; charts have no empty-state message (GAP-05).

### 11. Implementation status and outstanding gaps
Partially implemented (scatter, flow, cohort, Pareto, dossier, AM/vertical filters not built — GAP-16). Related register entries: GAP-16.

## 4.4 SCR-04 Sales & Marketing

### 1. Why the screen exists
Pipeline health is often judged on unweighted totals alone. Objective: Pipeline value, conversion, lead-source performance and loss reasons.

### 2. Who uses it
Sales leadership; marketing.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header + period chip
2. Row 1: KPI-SM-001…005
3. Row 2: CH-SM-001, CH-SM-002, CH-SM-003
4. Row 3: TB-SM-001
5. Footer note

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-SM-001 Open pipeline | Sum of estimated annual contract value of open opportunities (stage not closed) at range end. | $3.18M (Open pipeline at 2026-09-30) |
| KPI-SM-002 Weighted pipeline | Open pipeline weighted by stage probability. | $1.04M (Weighted pipeline at 2026-09-30) |
| KPI-SM-003 Win rate (closed in period) | Closed-won opportunities / (closed-won + closed-lost) closed in the range. | 31.4% (Closed in 2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-SM-004 Won value | Bookings won in the period (estimated annual contract value). | $901.7K (Won in 2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-SM-005 Avg quote turnaround (h) | Average hours from quote request to quote issued. | 10.0 (Hours, opportunities created in 2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-SM-006 Funnel stage reach | Where opportunities drop out. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| KPI-SM-007 Win rate by lead source | Which channels convert. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| KPI-SM-008 Loss reasons | Why deals are lost. | 35 (Lost in 2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| CH-SM-001 Conversion funnel | How many opportunities created in the period reached each stage. | - |
| CH-SM-002 Win rate by lead source | Which lead sources convert best. | - |
| CH-SM-003 Loss reasons | Why deals are lost. | - |
| TB-SM-001 Opportunities | Details of every opportunity. | - |

Interpretation notes: Win rate is by count; value_usd is an estimated annual contract value, not revenue.

### 5. What decision it supports
Is the pipeline sufficient, where do deals leak and why are they lost?

- KPI-SM-001 Open pipeline: Coverage of future bookings.
- KPI-SM-002 Weighted pipeline: Realistic bookings outlook.
- KPI-SM-003 Win rate (closed in period): Coach on lead sources or deal types that lose.
- KPI-SM-004 Won value: Compare bookings with revenue targets.
- KPI-SM-005 Avg quote turnaround (h): Address slow quoting.
- KPI-SM-006 Funnel stage reach: Target the leakiest stage.
- KPI-SM-007 Win rate by lead source: Shift marketing effort.
- KPI-SM-008 Loss reasons: Fix pricing, coverage or turnaround issues.

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-SM-001, KPI-SM-002, KPI-SM-003, KPI-SM-004, KPI-SM-005, KPI-SM-006, KPI-SM-007, KPI-SM-008, CH-SM-001, CH-SM-002, CH-SM-003, TB-SM-001 | fact_opportunity (+ fact_opportunity_stage_event) | fact_opportunity.closed_date, created_date, stage_current, value_usd, probability, lead_source, loss_reason, quote_turnaround_hours | public/data/fact_opportunity.csv, public/data/fact_opportunity_stage_event.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-SM-001 | Σ value_usd for opportunities with closed_date empty (open at the cut-off) | Opportunity state at 2026-09-30; Not applied: snapshot at the cut-off | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| KPI-SM-002 | Σ value_usd × probability over open opportunities | Opportunity state at 2026-09-30; Not applied: snapshot at the cut-off | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| KPI-SM-003 | COUNT(stage_current = CLOSED_WON) ÷ COUNT(closed_date in period), where closed = CLOSED_WON or CLOSED_LOST | closed_date; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Not applicable |
| KPI-SM-004 | Σ value_usd for CLOSED_WON opportunities with closed_date in period | closed_date; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| KPI-SM-005 | mean(quote_turnaround_hours) for opportunities with created_date in period (nulls ignored) | created_date; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Not applicable |
| KPI-SM-006 | For each stage in LEAD, QUALIFIED, PROPOSAL, NEGOTIATION, CLOSED_WON: COUNT DISTINCT opportunity_id with a stage event for that stage, among opportunities created in the period | created_date (cohort) and stage events; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Not applicable |
| KPI-SM-007 | Per lead_source: COUNT(CLOSED_WON) ÷ COUNT(closed in period) | closed_date; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Not applicable |
| KPI-SM-008 | COUNT of CLOSED_LOST opportunities closed in period, per loss_reason (empty → UNSPECIFIED) | closed_date; Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Not applicable |
| CH-SM-001 | Distinct opportunities created in period with a stage event per stage | closed_date or created_date (see formula); Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| CH-SM-002 | Per lead_source: won ÷ closed in period, rounded to 3 decimals | closed_date or created_date (see formula); Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| CH-SM-003 | COUNT of lost in period by loss_reason, descending | closed_date or created_date (see formula); Selected period (closed or created dates between the first day of the first month and day 31 of the last month) | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |
| TB-SM-001 | All fact_opportunity rows (not period-filtered); Close = closed_date or expected_close_date; ?stage= filters | closed_date or created_date (see formula); Not applied | Not applied (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter) | Money converted once from USD totals |

### 8. How it behaves
Filters: Range applies to closed/created-date metrics; open pipeline is a cut-off snapshot. Unit filter does not apply. Currency applies. Interactions: Table filter ?stage= (IE-P-04); no funnel click-through.

Expand analysis keys: KPI-SM-001 → analysis `sm:open`, KPI-SM-002 → analysis `sm:weighted`, KPI-SM-003 → analysis `sm:win`, KPI-SM-004 → analysis `sm:won`, KPI-SM-005 → analysis `sm:quote`, KPI-SM-006 → analysis `sm:win`, KPI-SM-007 → analysis `sm:win`, KPI-SM-008 → analysis `sm:loss`, CH-SM-001 → analysis `sm:win`, CH-SM-002 → analysis `sm:win`, CH-SM-003 → analysis `sm:loss`, TB-SM-001 → analysis `sm:open`.
Info icons: every listed component has one (texts in Appendix L). Tooltips on charts: see Section 6. Tables: search, sort, paging and CSV export (IE-G-18…22) unless stated.

### 9. How to validate it
| Component | Validation / reconciliation |
|---|---|
| KPI-SM-001 | Recompute from fact_opportunity rows with empty closed_date. |
| KPI-SM-002 | Probabilities come from a configured stage table (LEAD 10%, QUALIFIED 25%, PROPOSAL 45%, NEGOTIATION 70%). |
| KPI-SM-003 | Expand analysis shows won and closed counts. |
| KPI-SM-004 | value_usd is an estimated annual contract value, not recognised revenue. |
| KPI-SM-005 | Mean of non-null values. |
| KPI-SM-006 | Counts are non-increasing from LEAD to CLOSED_WON. |
| KPI-SM-007 | Weighted average of groups equals KPI-SM-003. |
| KPI-SM-008 | Sum equals lost count (35 YTD). |
| CH-SM-001 | - |
| CH-SM-002 | - |
| CH-SM-003 | - |
| TB-SM-001 | 216 rows without a stage filter. |

Screen acceptance: (1) Weighted pipeline = Σ value × probability of open opportunities. (2) Funnel counts are non-increasing. (3) Unit filter changes nothing on this tab.

### 10. What happens when data is missing or invalid
No closed deals → win rate n/a. Loading: skeleton (IE-G-27). Invalid dataset: 'Dataset unavailable' list (IE-G-28). Unexpected error: error boundary with 'Try again' (IE-G-26). Null ratios show 'n/a'; tables show 'No rows match the current filters.'; charts have no empty-state message (GAP-05).

Partially implemented (heatmap, MQL vs CAC, value win rate, cycle, filters not built — GAP-17). Related register entries: GAP-04, GAP-17.

Are we delivering on time, how much is AI-touched, and which active batches are at risk?

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |

| KPI-TR-001, KPI-TR-002, KPI-TR-003, KPI-TR-004, KPI-TR-005, KPI-TR-006, KPI-TR-007, CH-TR-001, CH-TR-002, TB-TR-001, CH-TR-003, PN-TR-001, TB-TR-002 | fact_translation_batch (+ fact_project for client, dim_client for unit) | fact_translation_batch.status, delivered_date, due_date, start_date, words_total, tm_match_words, workflow_id, client_rejected, project_id; fact_project.client_id | public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-TR-001 | TR_WORDS = Σ words_total for batches with status = DELIVERED and delivered month in the selected months | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-002 | Same as KPI-OV-006 | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-003 | TR_TAT = mean((delivered_date − start_date) in days) over delivered batches | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-004 | TM_REUSE = Σ tm_match_words ÷ Σ words_total, delivered batches | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-005 | REJECTION_RATE = COUNT(client_rejected = true) ÷ COUNT(delivered batches) | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-006 | For batches with status ≠ DELIVERED: Overdue if due_date < 2026-09-30; At risk if (due_date − 2026-09-30) ≤ 2 days and pct_complete < 0.8; otherwise On track (slaStatus in lib/kpi/rules.ts) | Snapshot at the cut-off; Not applied | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| KPI-TR-007 | Per lp_id over delivered batches in period: COUNT, Σ words_total, on-time ratio, mean turnaround, Σ words (workflow ≠ HT) ÷ Σ words | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| CH-TR-001 | Per delivery month: Σ words_total and on-time share (×100, 2 decimals) of batches delivered that month | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); All 33 months; BU applies | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| CH-TR-002 | Σ words_total of delivered batches in period per workflow_id | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| TB-TR-001 | Group delivered batches in period by lp_id; sorted by words descending | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Selected reporting period | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| CH-TR-003 | COUNT of batches with status ≠ DELIVERED (unit filter) per stage | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Not applied (cut-off snapshot) | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| PN-TR-001 | slaStatus() per active batch after ?lp= and ?stage= filters | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Not applied | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |
| TB-TR-002 | Active batches with slaStatus; ?lp= (pair label such as EN>ES) and ?stage= filter rows | Delivery month (month of delivered_date); Not applied | Applied via fact_project.client_id → dim_client.business_unit | Not applicable |

### 8. How it behaves
Filters: Range, currency and business unit all apply (except where a component says otherwise). The pipeline components are cut-off snapshots; trend charts show 33 months. Interactions: URL filters ?lp= and ?stage= affect the status panel and active-batch table only (IE-P-02).

## 4.7 SCR-07 Quality & Compliance

### 1. Why the screen exists
Quality evidence is scattered across review tools. Objective: Linguistic quality, error profile, disputes and corrective actions.

### 2. Who uses it
Quality and vendor managers.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header + period chip
2. Row 1: KPI-QC-001…005
3. Row 2: CH-QC-001 (left), CH-QC-002 (right)
4. Row 3: TB-QC-001
5. Footer note on the illustrative framework

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-QC-001 Quality score | Mean evaluation score on the single illustrative 0-100 framework (ILLUSTRATIVE_MQM_STYLE): 100 minus weighted error penalties per 1,000 sampled words (minor 1, major 5, critical 25). | 95.6 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-QC-002 Review pass rate | Evaluations with outcome PASS divided by all evaluations. | 92.7% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-QC-003 Errors per 1,000 words | Raw error density. | 3.1 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-QC-004 Open disputes | Evaluations with dispute_status = OPEN. | 2 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-QC-005 Open corrective actions | Backlog of quality remediation. | 4 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-QC-006 Errors by category and severity | Where errors cluster. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| CH-QC-001 Average quality score by month | Is quality stable over time? | - |
| CH-QC-002 Errors by category and severity | Which error categories dominate, and how severe they are. | - |
| TB-QC-001 Evaluations (latest 500 in period) | Detail of each evaluation. | - |

Interpretation notes: Score 0–100 = 100 − weighted penalties per 1,000 words (minor 1, major 5, critical 25). Pass = score ≥ 90 and no critical errors. Errors per 1,000 words is unweighted.

### 5. What decision it supports
Where do quality issues cluster and what remediation is open?

- KPI-QC-001 Quality score: As KPI-OV-009.
- KPI-QC-002 Review pass rate: Supplier review.
- KPI-QC-003 Errors per 1,000 words: Compare with the weighted quality score.
- KPI-QC-004 Open disputes: Resolve disputes.
- KPI-QC-005 Open corrective actions: Close or escalate actions.
- KPI-QC-006 Errors by category and severity: Target training (terminology, accuracy, …).

| CH-QC-002 | fact_quality_error, fact_quality_evaluation | fact_quality_evaluation.eval_date, score, outcome, dispute_status, corrective_action, corrective_status, critical_count, major_count, minor_count, sample_words, batch_id | public/data/fact_quality_error.csv, fact_quality_evaluation.csv |

Capacity planners; vendor managers.

| KPI-CD-003 Largest gap (words, 8 wks) | Scale of the worst shortfall. | 19.5K (Gap of the highest-load shortfall pair (EN>UR)) |

- KPI-CD-001 Forecast load, next 8 weeks: Source capacity in advance.

| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |

| KPI-CD-002 | COUNT(language pairs with Σ demand ÷ Σ supply > 1.0 over the first 8 forecast weeks) | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| KPI-CD-003 | max(0, demand − supply) of the first row of the shortfall list sorted by load (highest load), i.e. the gap of the highest-load pair | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| KPI-CD-004 | COUNT DISTINCT week_start with is_forecast = true | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| KPI-CD-005 | Per pair over the first 8 forecast weeks: load = Σ demand ÷ Σ supply; gap = max(0, Σ demand − Σ supply); status Shortfall > 1.0, Tight > 0.90, else OK | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| CH-CD-001 | Per week: Σ demand_words and Σ supply_words (all pairs, or the ?lp= pair); forecast bars at 55% opacity | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| CH-CD-002 | Cell = demand_words ÷ supply_words (2 decimals) per pair-week; colour scale 0.4–1.6 (light → yellow → orange → red) | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |
| TB-CD-001 | Per pair over the first 8 forecast weeks; sorted by load descending | week_start (13 actual weeks from 2026-06-29, 13 forecast weeks from 2026-09-28); Not applied: fixed 26-week window; KPIs use the first 8 forecast weeks | Not applied | Not applicable |

### 7. How the data is calculated

| KPI-FI-001 | Same as KPI-OV-001 | Recognition month (fact_revenue_line.month_id); Selected reporting period (whole months) | Applied through dim_client.business_unit | Converted once from the USD total: value ÷ dim_fx_rate.usd_per_unit |

| KPI-FI-006 | Per direct category (VENDOR_LINGUIST, INTERPRETER_PAY, MT_AI_TOOLING, PLATFORM_TELECOM, PM_DISPATCH_LABOR): −Σ amount_usd of direct costs attached to in-scope revenue lines; % of revenue = line ÷ REV | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |

| KPI-FI-008 | Same as KPI-EX-003 | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-FI-009 | Per service_line_id: revenue = Σ revenue_usd; direct = Σ direct cost; gross margin = (revenue − direct) ÷ revenue | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| KPI-FI-010 | Open balances (> $1) grouped by days past due at the cut-off: not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ | As at 2026-09-30 (invoice_date and payment_date ≤ cut-off); Not applied: fixed at the cut-off | Applied via client_id | Money converted once from USD totals |

| TB-FI-001 | Revenue; five direct categories (negative); Gross profit; three OPEX categories (negative, allocated); EBITDA | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |
| TB-FI-002 | Group in-scope revenue lines by service_line_id | Recognition month (month_id); Selected reporting period | Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share | Converted once from the USD total |

## 4.11 SCR-11 AI & Automation

### 1. Why the screen exists
AI benefits are often claimed without stated assumptions. Objective: AI adoption, quality estimation and assumption-based savings.

### 2. Who uses it
Executives; product and operations leaders.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header + period chip
2. Row 1: KPI-AI-001…005
3. Row 2: CH-AI-001 (left), CH-AI-002 (right)
4. Row 3: TB-AI-001 (left), PN-AI-001 (right)
5. Row 4: TB-AI-002
6. Footer note: savings are estimates

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-AI-001 AI-touched word share | Words in AI-touched workflows (MTPE or AIR) divided by delivered written words in the same range and population as TR_WORDS. | 44.0% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-AI-002 MTQE acceptance | Words whose segment-level quality-estimation score met the acceptance threshold (default 0.85) divided by AI-touched words in the same population. | 79.8% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-AI-003 Edit distance (words-weighted) | Word-weighted mean normalised edit distance on AI-touched batches (0 = unchanged, 1 = rewritten). Distinct from MTQE, BLEU and COMET. | 14.1% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-AI-004 Estimated hours saved | Estimate: words / baseline human words per hour minus words / observed words per hour. An estimate, not a measured result. | 2,626 (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-AI-005 Estimated cost saved | Estimate: hours saved x blended review hourly cost less tooling cost. | $74.9K (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| KPI-AI-006 Engine category metrics (table) | Compare generic synthetic engine categories. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| KPI-AI-007 Content sensitivity mix | Risk profile of AI-touched content. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| CH-AI-001 AI-touched share of delivered words | How AI adoption has grown. | - |
| CH-AI-002 Estimated savings by month | When estimated savings accrued. | - |
| TB-AI-001 By engine category | How synthetic engine categories compare. | - |
| PN-AI-001 Assumptions behind the savings estimate | What the savings estimate depends on. | - |
| TB-AI-002 Largest estimated savings (top 500 batches) | Which batches drive the estimate. | - |

Interpretation notes: QE score and edit distance are distinct; BLEU/COMET are not used. Savings are estimates from fixed assumptions.

### 5. What decision it supports
Is AI adoption growing, is machine output trustworthy, and what might it save?

- KPI-AI-001 AI-touched word share: As KPI-OV-008.
- KPI-AI-002 MTQE acceptance: Adjust review effort.
- KPI-AI-003 Edit distance (words-weighted): Engine selection.
- KPI-AI-004 Estimated hours saved: Business case for AI.
- KPI-AI-005 Estimated cost saved: Business case for AI.
- KPI-AI-006 Engine category metrics (table): Engine routing (illustrative only).
- KPI-AI-007 Content sensitivity mix: Governance of sensitive content.

| KPI-AI-002, KPI-AI-003, KPI-AI-004, KPI-AI-005, KPI-AI-006, KPI-AI-007, CH-AI-002, TB-AI-001, PN-AI-001, TB-AI-002 | fact_ai_workflow_batch (+ fact_translation_batch, fact_project) | fact_ai_workflow_batch.mtqe_score, mtqe_accepted_words, edit_distance, est_hours_saved, est_cost_saved_usd, engine_category, content_sensitivity, batch_id; fact_translation_batch.words_total, delivered_date | public/data/fact_ai_workflow_batch.csv, public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv |

Data and systems architects.

| KPI-TE-002 Error rate | SIMULATED: errors (4xx + 5xx + timeout) / requests. | 0.9% (90 days, all connectors (simulated)) |

Which simulated connectors are degraded?

| KPI-TE-006 | Σ errors_4xx, Σ errors_5xx, Σ errors_timeout over 90 days | date (90 days to 2026-09-30); Not applied: fixed 90 days | Not applied | Not applicable |

| TB-TE-001 | Group telemetry by connector | date (90 days to 2026-09-30); Not applied: fixed 90 days | Not applied | Not applicable |

## 4.13 SCR-13 Risk & Alerts

### 1. Why the screen exists
Alerts from different systems are not prioritised together. Objective: Rule-derived alerts with severity, exposure and recommended action.

### 2. Who uses it
Executives; operations; finance.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header
2. Row 1: KPI-RA-001…004
3. Row 2: CH-RA-001 (left), CH-RA-002 (right)
4. Row 3: TB-RA-001 alert list
5. Footer note on rule-based alerts

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-RA-001 Open alerts | Alerts in state OPEN or IN_PROGRESS (after local acknowledge/dismiss in the browser, which is not persisted). | 39 (Open or in-progress alerts) |
| KPI-RA-002 Critical + high | Urgent risks. | 17 (Open alerts, critical or high) |
| KPI-RA-003 Exposure (USD, indicative) | Indicative money at risk. | $170.1K (Indicative exposure of open alerts (USD)) |
| KPI-RA-004 Resolved | Closed alerts. | 1 (Resolved alerts) |
| KPI-RA-005 Risk matrix cell count | Distribution of risk. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| CH-RA-001 Open alerts by domain and severity | Which business domains carry the most and most severe alerts. | - |
| CH-RA-002 Risk matrix (open alerts) | How open alerts distribute by likelihood and impact. | - |
| TB-RA-001 Alert list | Every alert with its rule and recommended action. | - |

Interpretation notes: Alerts come from eight documented rules (R-SLA, R-HEALTH, R-CAP, R-DISP, R-CA, R-FX, R-AR60, R-CONN); exposures overlap and are not additive. Status values are assigned randomly by the generator.

### 5. What decision it supports
Which risks need action first?

- KPI-RA-001 Open alerts: Triage.
- KPI-RA-002 Critical + high: Escalation.
- KPI-RA-003 Exposure (USD, indicative): Prioritise by exposure.
- KPI-RA-004 Resolved: Context.
- KPI-RA-005 Risk matrix cell count: Focus on the high-likelihood, high-impact corner.

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-RA-001, KPI-RA-002, KPI-RA-003, KPI-RA-004, KPI-RA-005, CH-RA-001, CH-RA-002, TB-RA-001 | fact_risk_alert | fact_risk_alert.status, severity, domain, exposure_usd, likelihood, impact, rule_id | public/data/fact_risk_alert.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-RA-001 | COUNT(fact_risk_alert.status ≠ RESOLVED) | Snapshot at the cut-off; Not applied | Not applied | Not applied: always USD |

## 4.14 SCR-14 Forecasting & Scenarios

### 1. Why the screen exists
Forecasts are often presented without formulas. Objective: Transparent what-if analysis on the trailing-12-month baseline.

### 2. Who uses it
Executives; finance; interview reviewer.

### 3. What the user sees
1. Header
2. Browser-only notice
3. Left: Scenario drivers panel (presets, four sliders, reset)
4. Right: six result cards KPI-FS-001…006
5. Row 2: CH-FS-001 (left), CH-FS-002 (right)
6. Footer note on SCN-F1.0

### 4. What each component means
| Component | Meaning | Current value (default filters) |
|---|---|---|
| KPI-FS-001 Revenue (12 months) | Baseline TTM revenue x (1 + volume growth) x (1 + price adjustment). Transparent formula, versioned SCN-F1.0. | Baseline $1.37M; Conservative $1.28M; Optimistic $1.58M |
| KPI-FS-002 Gross margin | Scenario revenue less scenario direct costs (vendor cost re-priced with AI mix and inflation; PM labour semi-variable; platform variable) / scenario revenue. | Baseline 41.6%; Conservative 36.7%; Optimistic 44.6% |
| KPI-FS-003 EBITDA | Scenario EBITDA less baseline EBITDA; OPEX is semi-fixed (elasticity 0.25 to volume). | Baseline $192.1K; Conservative $94.3K; Optimistic $315.4K |
| KPI-FS-004 EBITDA margin | Operating margin under assumptions. | Baseline 14.0%; Conservative 7.4%; Optimistic 20.0% |
| KPI-FS-005 AI-touched word share | Adoption assumed in the scenario. | Baseline 43.8%; Conservative 46.8%; Optimistic 58.8% |
| KPI-FS-006 Capacity gap (words/yr) | Human words required (human-workflow words + AI words x 0.35 effort factor) less available human capacity words over 12 months. Positive = shortfall. | Baseline −3,303,394; Conservative −3,610,427; Optimistic −3,435,659 (negative = spare capacity) |
| KPI-FS-007 Revenue trajectory ranges | Range between conservative and optimistic preset scenarios. These are illustrative scenario ranges, NOT statistically validated confidence intervals. | Varies by segment; see validation rule |
| CH-FS-001 Baseline vs scenario | How the scenario changes the P&L. | - |
| CH-FS-002 Revenue trajectory ranges (next 12 months) | What revenue would look like at different growth rates. | - |

Interpretation notes: Results are illustrative scenario outputs, not statistical forecasts; the Baseline preset reproduces TTM EBITDA.

### 5. What decision it supports
What happens to revenue, margin, EBITDA and capacity if AI adoption, price, vendor cost or volume change?

- KPI-FS-001 Revenue (12 months): Compare strategies.
- KPI-FS-002 Gross margin: Pricing and AI trade-offs.
- KPI-FS-003 EBITDA: Investment decisions.
- KPI-FS-004 EBITDA margin: As KPI-FS-003.
- KPI-FS-005 AI-touched word share: AI rollout ambition.
- KPI-FS-006 Capacity gap (words/yr): Hiring vs AI adoption.
- KPI-FS-007 Revenue trajectory ranges: Frame growth ambition.

### 6. Where the data comes from
| Components | Source entity | Source fields | Source file(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-FS-001, KPI-FS-002, KPI-FS-003, KPI-FS-004, KPI-FS-005, KPI-FS-006, KPI-FS-007, CH-FS-001, CH-FS-002 | Baseline aggregates from fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line, fact_capacity_period; presets fact_scenario_assumption_set; parameters meta_config | revenue_usd, units, unit_type, workflow_id; cost_category, amount_usd; supply_words, is_forecast; scenario.* and assumptions.ai_effort_factor | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, fact_cost_line.csv, fact_capacity_period.csv, fact_scenario_assumption_set.csv, meta_config.csv |

### 7. How the data is calculated
| Component | Formula / logic | Period / date basis | Business unit | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-FS-001 | Rev′ = (Rw + Ri) × (1 + volume) × (1 + price) | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-002 | GM′ = GP′ ÷ Rev′; GP′ = Rev′ − vendor′ − tooling′ − interpreter pay′ − platform′ − labour′ | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-003 | EBITDA′ = GP′ − OPEX × (1 + 0.25 × volume) | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-004 | EM′ = EBITDA′ ÷ Rev′ | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-005 | a = clamp(a0 + AI adoption change, 0, 1); a0 = MTPE + AIR words ÷ all written words on trailing-12-month revenue lines | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-006 | Gap = W′ × ((1 − a) + 0.35 × a) − 52 × S; S = mean weekly actual supply_words (sum over pairs) | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| KPI-FS-007 | Month n (1..12) = avg monthly revenue of the last 12 months × (1 + r)^(n ÷ 12) ÷ fx, for r = 4% (conservative), 11% (target), 20% (aggressive) from meta_config.csv | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| CH-FS-001 | scenarioOutputs() for the Baseline preset and the current inputs; direct costs = revenue − GP; ÷ fx | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |
| CH-FS-002 | See KPI-FS-007; y-axis minimum = 90% of the lowest value | Trailing 12 months to 2026-09; Not applied: always trailing 12 months | Not applied: all business units | Money converted with the selected currency's fixed rate |

# 5. Complete KPI Dictionary

This section covers the 106 KPIs and metrics displayed in the application (cards, chart metrics, table metrics, panel figures and scenario outputs). Each displayed KPI links to its canonical definition in the KPI dictionary (`dim_kpi_definition.csv`, 81 entries, Appendix B) where one exists. Owner is 'Not assigned (demo)' throughout because no business owners are named in any source (DEC-09).

Refresh behaviour (all KPIs): values are recomputed on the server when the URL filters change or the page reloads; the dataset is re-read automatically when a CSV file changes (checked at most once per second) or on **Reload data**. Scenario KPIs recompute in the browser on every input change.

## 5.1 Overview

### KPI-OV-001 Revenue

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| KPI ID | KPI-OV-001 |
| KPI name (displayed label) | Revenue |
| Canonical dictionary ID | REV |
| Business definition | Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. Not bookings, invoices or cash. |
| Business purpose | Size of the business in the period on a recognised-revenue basis. |
| Decision supported | Decide whether growth is on track and which segment explains a change (via Expand analysis). |
| Unit | USD (or EUR/GBP) |
| Formula (as implemented) | REV = Σ fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd for lines with month_id in the selected months and client in the selected unit; displayed = REV ÷ fx(cur) |
| Numerator | - |
| Denominator | - |
| Aggregation | Sum |
| Data grain | Revenue line (one delivered written batch, or client x month x interpretation modality) |
| Source entity | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client for business unit) |
| Source fields | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id, service_line_id, unit_type, units; dim_client.business_unit |
| Source file | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| Transformation | Filter facts to the period and unit, join to dim_client (and fact_project for batch facts) for the unit, aggregate; money ÷ fx at display. Facts are aggregated separately before combining, so no join fan-out. |
| Time basis | Recognition month (fact_revenue_line.month_id) |
| Date range | Selected reporting period (whole months). Selectable: YTD, QTD, TTM, last 6/3 months, latest month, all data, custom months. |
| Filters (included / excluded) | Business unit: Applied through dim_client.business_unit. Zero / null rule: Empty set = 0. |
| Currency handling | Converted once from the USD total: value ÷ dim_fx_rate.usd_per_unit; fixed rates DEMO-FX-2026-09 (EUR 1.08, GBP 1.27 USD per unit) |
| Refresh behaviour | Server, on filter change / reload |
| Comparison | Compared with the prior period (YTD → same months of 2025; other ranges → equal-length window before; none for All data or before 2024-01). Ratios show the change in percentage points, other values a relative %. |
| Target direction / illustrative target | Higher / Plan = smoothed trend +3% (fact_kpi_target_period) |
| Tooltip explanation | Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. (full text: Appendix L, key `REV`) |
| Drill-down | Expand analysis `REV` |
| Current value (default filters) | $1.07M (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| Validation rule | Parity test: matches data/generated/kpi_reference.json (independent pandas) within 1e-9 relative (tests/parity.test.ts). Must equal Client & Revenue KPI-CR-001 and Finance KPI-FI-001 for the same filters (all use core()). |
| Owner | Not assigned (demo) |
| Status | Implemented |
| Notes | - |

### KPI-OV-002 Gross margin

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| KPI ID | KPI-OV-002 |
| KPI name (displayed label) | Gross margin |
| Canonical dictionary ID | GM |
| Business definition | Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. |
| Business purpose | Profitability of delivery before operating expenses. |
| Decision supported | Identify margin erosion by service line or tier. |
| Unit | Fraction (shown %) |
| Formula (as implemented) | GM = (REV − DIRECT) ÷ REV, where DIRECT = Σ fact_cost_line.amount_usd with cost_class = DIRECT attached (revenue_id) to the in-scope revenue lines |
| Numerator | GP |
| Denominator | REV |
| Aggregation | Ratio of sums |
| Data grain | Cost line (direct cost per revenue line and category; OPEX per month and category) |
| Source entity | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) |
| Source fields | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd |
| Source file | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| Transformation | Filter facts to the period and unit, join to dim_client (and fact_project for batch facts) for the unit, aggregate; money ÷ fx at display. Facts are aggregated separately before combining, so no join fan-out. |
| Time basis | Recognition month (month_id) |
| Date range | Selected reporting period. Selectable: YTD, QTD, TTM, last 6/3 months, latest month, all data, custom months. |
| Filters (included / excluded) | Business unit: Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share. Zero / null rule: REV = 0 -> N/A. |
| Currency handling | Converted once from the USD total; fixed rates DEMO-FX-2026-09 (EUR 1.08, GBP 1.27 USD per unit) |
| Refresh behaviour | Server, on filter change / reload |
| Comparison | Compared with the prior period (YTD → same months of 2025; other ranges → equal-length window before; none for All data or before 2024-01). Ratios show the change in percentage points, other values a relative %. |
| Target direction / illustrative target | Higher / >= 38% |
| Tooltip explanation | Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. (full text: Appendix L, key `GM`) |
| Drill-down | Expand analysis `GM` |
| Current value (default filters) | 42.1% (2026-01 to 2026-09) |
| Validation rule | Parity test: matches data/generated/kpi_reference.json (independent pandas) within 1e-9 relative (tests/parity.test.ts). |
| Owner | Not assigned (demo) |
| Status | Implemented |
| Notes | - |

### KPI-OV-003 EBITDA margin

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| KPI ID | KPI-OV-003 |
| KPI name (displayed label) | EBITDA margin |
| Canonical dictionary ID | EBITDA_M |
| Business definition | EBITDA / recognised revenue. |
| Business purpose | Operating profitability after allocated operating expenses. |
| Decision supported | Judge whether growth converts into operating profit. |
| Unit | Fraction |
| Formula (as implemented) | EBITDA_M = (GP − OPEX_alloc) ÷ REV; OPEX_alloc = Σ OPEX of the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV) |
| Numerator | EBITDA |
| Denominator | REV |
| Aggregation | Ratio of sums |

# 6. Chart and Visualization Dictionary

33 charts, 22 data tables and 4 panels. All charts are Apache ECharts rendered by `components/EChart.tsx` on a canvas, loaded on demand, with the shared theme (teal, red, navy, green, amber, blue, slate), animation off and legends at the top.

## 6.1 Overview

### CH-OV-001 Revenue and EBITDA by month

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID and title | CH-OV-001 — Revenue and EBITDA by month |
| Screen and location | SCR-01 Overview; Row 2, left |
| Business question | How revenue and operating profit moved over 33 months, including seasonality. |
| Why this type | Bars show volume per month; a line on the same axis shows how much of each month's revenue remains after all costs. |
| Type | Combined bar (revenue) + line (EBITDA) |
| X-axis | Month (2024-01 … 2026-09) |
| Y-axis | Amount in selected currency |
| Series / legend | Revenue (bars), EBITDA (line) |
| Underlying metrics / KPI IDs | KPI-OV-001, KPI-OV-003 |
| Dimensions, grouping, aggregation | monthlySeries(bu): per month Σ revenue_usd and Σ direct cost of in-scope lines; OPEX(month) × unit revenue share; EBITDA = revenue − direct − OPEX; values ÷ fx, rounded to whole units |
| Source entities | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) |
| Source fields | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd |
| Source files | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv |
| Default date range and filters | All 33 months regardless of range; BU applies. Business unit: Applied via the client; company OPEX is allocated by the unit's revenue share. Currency: Converted once from the USD total. |
| Sorting / ranking | Category order as listed |
| Tooltip | Axis tooltip: category label and each series value, formatted by the chart's format (money uses the selected currency symbol). |
| Click, hover, selection, cross-filter | Hover shows the tooltip; clicking a chart element does nothing (no cross-filter or drill-through). |
| Expand-to-detail | Expand icon opens a full-screen dialog containing the live chart (taller, with 'Show data table'), then loads analysis `EBITDA` from /api/analysis with the page's URL filters (stats, trend, breakdowns with drill-down, insights, 'Not available' notes, definition). Filters persist because they are read from the URL. Close, Escape or a click on the backdrop returns to the dashboard; focus returns to the expand button. |
| Empty, invalid, error states | No explicit empty state: an empty series draws empty axes. If the dataset fails validation the page shows 'Dataset unavailable' instead. |
| Accessibility and responsive behaviour | role=img with an aria-label; width follows the card (ResizeObserver); taller in the expanded view, which also offers 'Show data table' (except heatmap and scatter). |
| Info icon | Yes — key `ov.revEbitda` (Appendix L) |
| Validation and acceptance | Σ revenue over the selected months equals KPI-OV-001. |
| Status | Implemented |
| Notes | - |

## 7.2 Information (i) icons — what each one displays

Each icon shows the entry below. The tooltip (hover/focus) shows the title and summary; the full panel adds the remaining sections. The complete texts are reproduced verbatim in Appendix L.

Page-level overrides (added by the page, in addition to the dictionary text): NRR cards add the fixed-window caveat and a 'mismatch' basis; DSO cards add the cut-off caveat and 'mismatch' basis; EBITDA margin (Overview, Finance) and EBITDA (Executive) add the OPEX-allocation caveat; Estimated hours/cost saved add 'assumption-driven estimate'. KPI cards with a prior comparison append the standard comparison text: "Compared with the prior period: for Year to date, the same months of 2025; for other ranges, the window of equal length immediately before the selected one. No comparison for All data, or when that window would start before 2024-01. The change is shown in percentage points (pp) [ratios] / as a relative % change [others]. Green marks a move in the favourable direction, red the opposite."
