# 8. Business Rules and Metric Definitions

**How to read the status column.** No definition has been formally approved (the BRD is a draft). "Implemented — dictionary" means the rule is written in the KPI dictionary (`dim_kpi_definition.csv`, from `scripts/kpi_catalog.py`) **and** the code follows it. "Implemented — code only" means the code applies the rule but no dictionary entry states it. "Proposed" and "TBD" entries are recommendations or open questions, not decisions.

## 8.1 Money concepts

| ID | Rule | Definition as implemented | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-REV-01 | Recognised revenue | Written work is recognised in the month the batch is delivered (one revenue line per delivered batch: words × price); interpretation in the service month (one line per client × month × modality: fulfilled minutes × price). `revenue_usd = round_half_up(revenue_original × fx_usd_per_unit, 2)`. Reported revenue = Σ revenue_usd of lines whose `month_id` is in the selected months. | Implemented — dictionary (REV) | generate_synthetic_data.py build_finance; core() |
| BRL-REV-02 | Invoiced revenue | Billed in arrears: one invoice line per client × service line × revenue month, dated the 3rd of the following month; `amount = Σ revenue_original × (1 + adjustment_fraction)` where 93% of lines have no adjustment, 4% a credit of 1–5% and 3% an uplift of 0.5–3%. Invoices dated after the cut-off are not generated. Invoiced value is **not** used as revenue anywhere. | Implemented — code only | build_invoices |
| BRL-REV-03 | Cash collected | One payment per invoice (all lines), dated invoice date + payment terms + a client-specific slip + noise (minimum 7 days); 2% of payments short-pay the first line at 95%. Payments after the cut-off are not generated. Cash is never shown as revenue; it is used only to compute receivables. | Implemented — code only | build_invoices |
| BRL-AR-01 | Accounts receivable | Open balance of an invoice line at date E = amount_usd − Σ allocated_usd of payments with payment_date ≤ E, for invoices with invoice_date ≤ E. Views exclude balances of $1 or less. **Overdue** = open balance on a line whose due_date is before 2026-09-30. Aging buckets by days past due: not yet due (≤ 0), 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+. | Implemented — code only (DSO is in the dictionary) | receivables() in lib/kpi/core.ts; finance page |
| BRL-AR-02 | DSO | DSO = open AR at E × 90 ÷ amount invoiced in the 90 days to E (E − 89 days … E). E is fixed at 2026-09-30 in the app; the dictionary says "range end" (CNF-03). Payment terms: Strategic 60, Growth 45, Standard 30 days. | Implemented — dictionary (window differs) | dso() |
| BRL-BKG-01 | Bookings vs revenue | `fact_opportunity.value_usd` is an **estimated annual contract value**. Open pipeline, weighted pipeline and won value are bookings-type measures and are never added to recognised revenue. Probability is a configured stage table (LEAD 0.10, QUALIFIED 0.25, PROPOSAL 0.45, NEGOTIATION 0.70, WON 1, LOST 0). | Implemented — dictionary (PIPE_UNW, PIPE_W) | build_opportunities; sales page |

## 8.2 Costs, profit and margins

| ID | Rule | Definition as implemented | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-PL-01 | Direct costs | Cost class DIRECT, attached to a revenue line: VENDOR_LINGUIST (assigned words × resource rate × role factor), INTERPRETER_PAY (minutes × interpreter rate × language factor × 1.35 for on-site), MT_AI_TOOLING (AI words × $0.004 × engine factor), PLATFORM_TELECOM (minutes × modality rate), PM_DISPATCH_LABOR (7% of written revenue, 5% of interpretation revenue, ± noise). Costs are USD only. | Implemented — dictionary (DIRECT_COST) |
| BRL-PL-02 | Operating expenses | Cost class OPEX per month: SALES_MARKETING ≈ 9.5%, TECHNOLOGY_PRODUCT ≈ 7.5%, GENERAL_ADMIN ≈ 11.5% of the trailing-3-month average revenue. With a business unit selected, OPEX is allocated by the unit's share of revenue in the selected months. | Implemented — dictionary (OPEX) |
| BRL-PL-03 | Depreciation and amortisation | Cost class DA per month ≈ 2.2% of the trailing-6-month average revenue; recorded below EBITDA; computed by core() as DA but **not shown** on any tab (DEC-10). | Implemented — code only |
| BRL-PL-04 | Gross profit and gross margin | GP = REV − DIRECT for the same revenue lines; GM = GP ÷ REV (N/A when REV = 0). | Implemented — dictionary (GP, GM) |
| BRL-PL-05 | EBITDA and EBITDA margin | EBITDA = GP − OPEX (allocated); EBITDA margin = EBITDA ÷ REV. Interest and tax are out of scope. | Implemented — dictionary (EBITDA, EBITDA_M) |
| BRL-PL-06 | Operating margin | Not defined. EBITDA margin is the only operating-level margin; "operating margin" (EBIT ÷ revenue) would also deduct D&A. | TBD — Business Decision Required. Proposed: do not show "operating margin" unless D&A is included as EBIT. |
| BRL-PL-07 | Service-line profitability | Per service line: revenue, direct cost, GM (TB-FI-002). OPEX is not allocated to service lines on the dashboard (the Expand analysis allocates it pro-rata for segment EBITDA). | Implemented — code only |
| BRL-PL-08 | Client profitability | Not shown. Could be computed per client from direct costs attached to the client's revenue lines. | Planned (BRD 6.10 ledger); proposed formula: client GM = (Σ revenue_usd − Σ direct cost) ÷ Σ revenue_usd per client_id. |
| BRL-PL-09 | Vendor COGS share, revenue and cost per word | (VENDOR_LINGUIST + INTERPRETER_PAY) ÷ REV; written revenue ÷ written units; vendor linguist cost ÷ written units. Computed by core(), **not displayed**. | Implemented in the KPI layer only |

## 8.3 Classification rules

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-SL-01 | Service lines are mutually exclusive | Six service lines: TRANSLATION, LOCALIZATION, ALT_FORMAT (written, billed per word) and OPI, VRI, ONSITE (interpretation, billed per minute). Each revenue line has exactly one. Revenue by service line sums to total revenue (generator check R-REV-1). | Implemented — dictionary and generator check |
| BRL-WF-01 | Workflow is not a revenue category | Written batches carry a workflow: HT (human), MTPE (machine translation post-editing), AIR (AI-assisted review). AI-touched = MTPE + AIR. Workflows never appear in dim_service_line (generator check R-SL), so MTPE cannot be double counted as revenue. ALT_FORMAT work is always HT. | Implemented — dictionary and generator check |
| BRL-WF-02 | Eligible translation population | Words, MTPE share, AI share, TM reuse and rejection rate all use delivered batches whose delivery month is in the selected months (same population). | Implemented — dictionary |

## 8.4 Workforce, utilisation and capacity

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-HC-01 | Active resources | dim_resource.is_active = true (no termination at the cut-off). Includes freelance and internal linguists and interpreters. | Implemented — dictionary (TALENT_POOL) |
| BRL-HC-02 | Headcount and FTE | Internal FTE (internal resources + active owners) is defined in the dictionary (INTERNAL_FTE) but not shown. No FTE fraction (part-time) is modelled. | Planned; TBD whether FTE should count owners. |
| BRL-UTIL-01 | PM utilisation | Allocated PM hours (est_pm_hours spread evenly over each project's start..due days, counted inside the window) ÷ available hours (38 h/week × days employed in the window ÷ 7) for PROJECT_MANAGER owners. Dictionary direction: target band 70–90%; warning above 90%. | Implemented — dictionary (colour signal differs, GAP-08) |
| BRL-CAP-01 | Capacity load and status | Load = Σ demand_words ÷ Σ supply_words over the window (words for both). Supply = Σ linguist weekly capacity × availability for the pair. Status per pair over the first 8 forecast weeks: Shortfall > 100%, Tight > 90%, OK otherwise. | Implemented — dictionary (CAP_LOAD); count threshold differs (CNF-06) |

## 8.5 Delivery and quality

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-OTD-01 | Turnaround and on-time delivery | Turnaround = calendar days from batch start_date to delivered_date. On time = delivered_date ≤ due_date. Population: delivered batches in the period (in-progress batches excluded). | Implemented — dictionary (TR_TAT, TR_OTD) |
| BRL-SLA-01 | SLA status of active batches | Overdue: due_date before 2026-09-30. At risk: due within 2 days of the cut-off and pct_complete below 80%. Otherwise on track. Thresholds sla_warning_days and sla_warning_progress in meta_config.csv. | Implemented — code (rules.ts); dictionary SLA_RISK |
| BRL-FILL-01 | Interpretation denominators | Minutes: FULFILLED only. Fill rate: FULFILLED ÷ (FULFILLED + UNFULFILLED); cancellations by the client and technical failures are excluded. VRI connection success: FULFILLED ÷ (FULFILLED + TECH_FAILURE) for VRI. ASA: fulfilled on-demand OPI only. | Implemented — dictionary |
| BRL-QS-01 | Quality score | Single illustrative framework (ILLUSTRATIVE_MQM_STYLE): score = max(0, 100 − (minor × 1 + major × 5 + critical × 25) × 1,000 ÷ sample_words). PASS when score ≥ 90 and no critical errors. | Implemented — dictionary (QUALITY_SCORE, REVIEW_PASS) |
| BRL-QS-02 | Defect rate | "Errors per 1,000 words" = unweighted error count ÷ sampled words × 1,000. | Implemented — code only |
| BRL-QS-03 | Rework rate | Not defined. The closest measure is client rejection rate (rejected delivered batches ÷ delivered batches). | TBD — Business Decision Required. Proposed: rework rate = batches with client_rejected or a FAIL evaluation ÷ delivered batches. |
| BRL-HLT-01 | Client health | 0.30 × on-time delivery (90 days) + 0.25 × quality ((score − 80) ÷ 20, clipped 0..1) + 0.20 × payment timeliness (share of invoices due in 180 days paid within terms) + 0.25 × revenue trend (last 3 months ÷ prior 3 months − 0.5, clipped 0..1); weights re-normalised when a component is missing. Bands: HEALTHY ≥ 0.70, WATCH ≥ 0.50, else AT_RISK. Snapshots at quarter-ends and the cut-off month. | Implemented — dictionary (HEALTH) |
| BRL-NRR-01 | NRR and churn | Cohort = clients with revenue > 0 in the opening 12 months (months e−23 … e−12); NRR = cohort revenue in the latest 12 months ÷ opening revenue; gross revenue churn = Σ max(0, opening − latest) ÷ Σ opening (revenue-based); logo churn = cohort clients with no latest revenue ÷ cohort; logo retention = 1 − logo churn. e = 2026-09 in the app. | Implemented — dictionary (window differs, CNF-03) |

## 8.6 Comparisons, targets and time

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-PER-01 | Reporting period | Whole calendar months only, 2024-01 … 2026-09 (33 months). Presets and Custom as in IE-G-01/02. Invalid values fall back to Year to date. | Implemented — code (lib/filters.ts) |
| BRL-PER-02 | Period-over-period and year-over-year | Year to date compares with the same months of the previous year (a year-over-year comparison). Other ranges compare with the equal-length window immediately before. None for All data or when the window would start before 2024-01. Ratios show the change in percentage points; other values a relative % change. Green = favourable direction for that KPI. | Implemented — code (priorMonths, delta()) |
| BRL-TGT-01 | Plan and targets | Monthly REV plan = centred 5-month rolling mean of actual monthly revenue × 1.03 (generated from actuals, so it is illustrative). Flat monthly targets: GM 40%, EBITDA margin 13%, OTD 95%, on-demand fill 95%, quality 92. Revenue target over a period = Σ monthly plan (× unit revenue share when a unit is selected); ratio targets = mean of monthly targets. Attainment = actual ÷ target; On target ≥ 100%, Near ≥ 97%, else Behind. | Implemented — code (differs from REV_VS_PLAN, CNF-02) |
| BRL-TGT-02 | Forecast vs actual, budget vs actual | No budget exists. No forecast is compared with actuals (forecast weeks are in the future; trajectories start after the cut-off). | TBD — Business Decision Required. Proposed: treat fact_kpi_target_period as the plan of record and label it "plan", not "budget". |

## 8.7 Currency

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-FX-01 | Reporting currency | Canonical currency USD. Fixed illustrative rates DEMO-FX-2026-09: 1 EUR = 1.08 USD, 1 GBP = 1.27 USD (dim_fx_rate.csv). Displayed amount = USD total ÷ rate, applied once to aggregated totals; rounding only for display. Revenue, invoices and payments also store the original currency and the rate used; costs are USD only. Always USD regardless of the selector: alert exposure, OKR money values, resource rates, AI assumptions panel. Not live FX. | Implemented — dictionary conventions and code |
| BRL-FX-02 | FX exposure | Alert rule R-FX: exposure = 10% of open EUR or GBP receivables (USD equivalent). | Implemented — generator rule |

## 8.8 Missing, cancelled, refunded, duplicate and late data

| ID | Situation | Handling as implemented | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-DQ-01 | Invalid data | Every CSV is validated on load against meta_fields.csv and meta_tables.csv (header order, types, required values, allowed values, 0..1 and −1..1 ranges, real calendar dates, primary keys including composite keys, foreign keys, empty required tables) plus app checks (calendar, cut-off, FX rate for every currency, required config sections). **Any problem blocks all dashboards** ("Dataset unavailable"); invalid rows are excluded and reported. | Implemented — code |
| BRL-DQ-02 | Missing values | Nullable fields per the dictionary (e.g. delivered_date for in-progress batches, connect_seconds for scheduled sessions). Means and ratios ignore missing values where the formula requires; an empty denominator returns null, shown as "n/a". | Implemented |
| BRL-DQ-03 | Cancellations | CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT sessions are excluded from minutes and fill rates; TECH_FAILURE sessions are excluded from fill rates and counted in the VRI connection denominator. | Implemented — dictionary |
| BRL-DQ-04 | Refunds and credits | No refunds are modelled. Credits and uplifts exist only as invoice `adjustment_fraction`; recognised revenue is not adjusted. | TBD — Business Decision Required (DEC-11) |
| BRL-DQ-05 | Duplicates | Duplicate primary keys are reported ("Duplicate IDs"), later duplicates excluded and the dataset blocked. | Implemented — code |
| BRL-DQ-06 | Late-arriving data | Not modelled: the dataset is a closed snapshot at 2026-09-30. Replacing CSV files reloads everything (no incremental loads or restatement history). | TBD — needed before real data is connected |

## 8.9 AI, alerts and scenarios

| ID | Rule | Definition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRL-AI-01 | AI savings estimate | Hours saved per AI batch = words ÷ 380 − words ÷ observed words per hour; cost impact = hours × $32 − tooling cost. MTQE acceptance threshold 0.85. QE score, edit distance, BLEU and COMET are never mixed (BLEU/COMET not used). An estimate, not a measured saving. | Implemented — dictionary |
| BRL-ALR-01 | Alert rules | R-SLA (overdue or at-risk batches; CRITICAL when overdue with estimated revenue > $1,500), R-HEALTH (clients AT_RISK), R-CAP (8-week load > 90%; CRITICAL > 110%, HIGH > 100%), R-DISP (open disputes), R-CA (corrective actions open > 45 days), R-FX (non-USD receivables), R-AR60 (receivables > 60 days past due), R-CONN (7-day simulated uptime < 99.5%). Status values are randomly assigned for the demo. | Implemented — generator (assemble.py build_alerts) |
| BRL-SCN-01 | Scenario engine | SCN-F1.0 formulas (Section 12) on the trailing-12-month baseline; elasticities and the AI effort factor from meta_config.csv. | Implemented — dictionary (SCN_*) |
| BRL-SCN-02 | Forecast range wording | Ranges are "illustrative scenario ranges", never "confidence intervals". | Implemented — UI text and dictionary (FORECAST_RANGE) |

# 9. Data Lineage and Data Model Mapping

## 9.1 End-to-end lineage

```
Generator inputs: scripts/config.py (seed, thresholds, assumptions, FX) · scripts/schema.py (tables,
                  fields, enums) · scripts/kpi_catalog.py (81 KPI definitions)
        │
        ▼
scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py + scripts/assemble.py ── validate.py: 864 checks (stops on a critical failure)
        ├──► public/data/*.csv (36 data tables + meta_tables, meta_fields, meta_dataset, meta_config)
        └──► data/generated/kpi_reference.json (independent pandas values for the parity tests)
        │
        ▼
lib/data/csv.ts → loader.ts (validate against meta_*) → store.ts (cache, app checks, derived indexes)
        │
        ▼
lib/kpi/core.ts · agg.ts · rules.ts · lib/scenario.ts · lib/analysis/engine.ts · lib/info/registry.ts
        │
        ▼
app/(app)/<tab>/page.tsx (server) → client components (EChart, DataTable, InfoTip, ExpandAnalysis) → browser
```

No external source is connected. Every file is synthetic or, for telemetry, simulated.

## 9.2 Entity relationship overview

Read `A ──< B` as 'one A has many B'; `B >── C` as 'many B reference one C'.

```
dim_owner ──< dim_client
dim_client ──< fact_project ──< fact_translation_batch ──< fact_resource_assignment >── dim_resource
fact_translation_batch ──< fact_ai_workflow_batch          (delivered MTPE / AIR batches only)
fact_translation_batch ──< fact_quality_evaluation ──< fact_quality_error
dim_resource ──< bridge_resource_language >── dim_language_pair
dim_client ──< fact_interpretation_session >── dim_resource (interpreter)
dim_client ──< fact_revenue_line ──< fact_cost_line (DIRECT)       fact_cost_line (OPEX, DA) per month
dim_client ──< fact_invoice_line ──< bridge_payment_invoice >── fact_payment
dim_client ──< fact_client_period_snapshot
fact_opportunity ──< fact_opportunity_stage_event
dim_language_pair ──< fact_capacity_period
dim_connector ──< fact_integration_telemetry
dim_owner ──< fact_risk_alert, fact_okr            dim_kpi_definition ──< fact_kpi_target_period, fact_okr
fact_scenario_assumption_set ──< fact_scenario_output
dim_date (month) ──< fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line, fact_invoice_line, fact_kpi_target_period, snapshots
```

Relationships that matter for calculations:

- **Financial:** revenue lines carry the client and service line; direct cost lines point to a revenue line (revenue_id), so gross profit is computed per revenue line without a join fan-out. OPEX and D&A are monthly and company-level (allocated by revenue share for a unit). Invoices aggregate revenue per client × service line × month; payments are allocated to invoice lines through the bridge, which yields receivables.
- **Operational:** a project belongs to one client and service line; its batches carry language pair and workflow. The client (and therefore business unit) of a batch, evaluation or AI batch is reached through fact_project. Interpretation sessions carry the client directly.
- **Client:** dim_client.business_unit drives the unit filter; tier and vertical drive breakdowns; snapshots hold health scores.
- **Workforce:** dim_resource is linked to batches through assignments and to sessions as interpreter; capacity supply comes from linguist capacity × availability per language pair.
- **Forecasting:** the scenario baseline aggregates revenue lines, cost lines and actual capacity weeks; presets come from fact_scenario_assumption_set; Python reference outputs are stored in fact_scenario_output.

## 9.4 Lineage matrix for every KPI and chart

Pattern: Screen → Component → KPI / Metric → Calculation → Source Entity → Source Fields → Source File → Transformation.

| Screen | Component | KPI / metric | Calculation | Source entity | Source fields | Source file | Transformation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-001 | Revenue | REV = Σ fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd for lines with month_id in the selected months and client in the selected unit; displayed = REV ÷ fx(cur) | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client for business unit) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id, service_line_id, unit_type, units; dim_client.business_unit | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-002 | Gross margin | GM = (REV − DIRECT) ÷ REV, where DIRECT = Σ fact_cost_line.amount_usd with cost_class = DIRECT attached (revenue_id) to the in-scope revenue lines | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-003 | EBITDA margin | EBITDA_M = (GP − OPEX_alloc) ÷ REV; OPEX_alloc = Σ OPEX of the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV) | fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id; fact_cost_line.cost_class, cost_category, revenue_id, month_id, amount_usd | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/fact_cost_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-004 | Active clients | COUNT DISTINCT client_id whose Σ revenue_usd in the selected months > 0 | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client for business unit) | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd, month_id, client_id, service_line_id, unit_type, units; dim_client.business_unit | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-005 | Net revenue retention (TTM) | Cohort = clients with revenue > 0 in 2024-10..2025-09; NRR = Σ cohort revenue 2025-10..2026-09 ÷ Σ cohort revenue 2024-10..2025-09 | fact_revenue_line (+ dim_client) | fact_revenue_line.client_id, month_id, revenue_usd; dim_client.business_unit | public/data/fact_revenue_line.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-006 | Translation on-time delivery | TR_OTD = COUNT(delivered batches with delivered_date ≤ due_date) ÷ COUNT(delivered batches), delivered in the selected months | fact_translation_batch (+ fact_project for client, dim_client for unit) | fact_translation_batch.status, delivered_date, due_date, start_date, words_total, tm_match_words, workflow_id, client_rejected, project_id; fact_project.client_id | public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-007 | OPI speed to answer | OPI_ASA = mean(connect_seconds) over sessions with service_line_id = OPI, request_type = ON_DEMAND, status = FULFILLED | fact_interpretation_session (+ dim_client) | fact_interpretation_session.request_date, status, service_line_id, request_type, duration_min, connect_seconds, client_id | public/data/fact_interpretation_session.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-008 | AI-touched word share | AI_SHARE = Σ words_total (workflow_id ≠ HT) ÷ Σ words_total, delivered batches in the selected months | fact_translation_batch (+ fact_project for client, dim_client for unit) | fact_translation_batch.status, delivered_date, due_date, start_date, words_total, tm_match_words, workflow_id, client_rejected, project_id; fact_project.client_id | public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv, public/data/dim_client.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |
| SCR-01 Overview | KPI-OV-009 | Quality score | QUALITY_SCORE = mean(fact_quality_evaluation.score) for evaluations in the selected months; score = max(0, 100 − (minor×1 + major×5 + critical×25) × 1000 ÷ sample_words) | fact_quality_evaluation (+ fact_translation_batch → fact_project for client) | fact_quality_evaluation.eval_date, score, outcome, dispute_status, corrective_action, corrective_status, critical_count, major_count, minor_count, sample_words, batch_id | public/data/fact_quality_evaluation.csv, public/data/fact_translation_batch.csv, public/data/fact_project.csv | Filter to period/unit → aggregate per fact → combine → ÷ fx for money |

# 10. User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

70 stories. Stories marked 'Not implemented' describe BRD scope that is not built and are kept so the gap is traceable. Acceptance criteria are numbered `<story>-AC<n>`.

## 10.1 Login

### US-LG-001 Login form

**As a** Signed-in demo user, **I want** to sign in with the demo username and a private password, **so that** only authorised viewers can see the demo dashboards.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story ID | US-LG-001 |
| Screen / component | SCR-LG Login / Login form |
| Persona | Signed-in demo user |
| Business need | Only authorised viewers can see the demo dashboards. |
| Preconditions | User is not signed in. |
| Main success flow | User opens /login, enters credentials and submits. |
| Alternate flows | An already signed-in user who opens /login is redirected to /overview. |
| Error and exception flows | Wrong or missing credentials show a generic message; the server never reveals which field was wrong. |
| Business rules | BRL-SEC-01, BRL-SEC-02 |
| Related KPI IDs | - |
| Related chart / table IDs | - |
| Data dependencies | Environment variables only |
| Priority | Must |
| Dependencies | - |
| Requirement links | FR-11, BR-06 |
| Implementation status | Implemented |
| Test cases | TC-AUTH-03, TC-SEC-01, TC-SEC-02 |

Acceptance criteria:

- **US-LG-001-AC1** — **Given** valid DEMO_USERNAME, DEMO_PASSWORD and SESSION_SECRET (≥ 32 characters) are configured, **When** the user submits the correct username and password, **Then** an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie valid for 8 hours is set and the browser goes to /overview.
- **US-LG-001-AC2** — **Given** the server is configured, **When** the user submits a wrong password, **Then** 'Invalid username or password.' is shown, the username stays filled in and no cookie is set.
- **US-LG-001-AC3** — **Given** DEMO_PASSWORD or SESSION_SECRET is missing or the secret is shorter than 32 characters, **When** the user submits the form, **Then** 'Sign-in is not configured on this server.' is shown.

### US-LG-002 Route protection

**As a** Signed-in demo user, **I want** to be redirected to the login page when my session is missing, expired or tampered with, **so that** protected data is never shown without a valid session.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story ID | US-LG-002 |
| Screen / component | SCR-LG Login / Route protection |
| Persona | Signed-in demo user |
| Business need | Protected data is never shown without a valid session. |
| Preconditions | - |
| Main success flow | proxy.ts verifies the HMAC-signed cookie on every request except /login and static assets; the dashboard layout verifies it again. |
| Alternate flows | - |
| Error and exception flows | If the CSV dataset fails validation, the page shows 'Dataset unavailable' with the problem list instead of any figure. |
| Business rules | BRL-SEC-02, BRL-SEC-03 |
| Related KPI IDs | - |
| Related chart / table IDs | - |
| Data dependencies | Session cookie bls_oneview_session; SESSION_SECRET |
| Priority | Must |
| Dependencies | - |
| Requirement links | FR-11, FR-12 |
| Implementation status | Implemented |
| Test cases | TC-AUTH-01, TC-AUTH-02, TC-AUTH-04, TC-AUTH-05 |

Acceptance criteria:

- **US-LG-002-AC1** — **Given** no session cookie, **When** the user requests any dashboard route, **Then** the server responds with a redirect (307) to /login.
- **US-LG-002-AC2** — **Given** an expired, wrongly signed or malformed cookie, **When** the user requests /overview, **Then** the user is redirected to /login and the bad cookie is deleted.
- **US-LG-002-AC3** — **Given** no session, **When** a client calls GET /api/analysis or GET/POST /api/data, **Then** the API returns 401 'Not signed in'.

### US-LG-003 Sign out

**As a** Signed-in demo user, **I want** to sign out, **so that** the shared demo session ends on this device.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story ID | US-LG-003 |
| Screen / component | SCR-LG Login / Sign out |
| Persona | Signed-in demo user |
| Business need | The shared demo session ends on this device. |
| Preconditions | User is signed in; the dataset passed validation. |
| Main success flow | 1. User uses the shared shell; global filters are read from the URL. 2. The server validates the session and the dataset, computes the 'Sign out' figures with the shared KPI layer and renders them. 3. User reads the values, hovers the info icons for definitions and, where available, opens Expand analysis for detail. |
| Alternate flows | - |
| Error and exception flows | If the CSV dataset fails validation, the page shows 'Dataset unavailable' with the problem list instead of any figure. |
| Business rules | - |
| Related KPI IDs | - |
| Related chart / table IDs | - |
| Data dependencies | Session cookie bls_oneview_session |
| Priority | Must |
| Dependencies | - |
| Requirement links | FR-12 |
| Implementation status | Implemented |
| Test cases | TC-AUTH-03 |

Acceptance criteria:

- **US-LG-003-AC1** — **Given** the user is signed in, **When** the user clicks Sign out, **Then** the session cookie is deleted and /login is shown.
- **US-LG-003-AC2** — **Given** the user has signed out, **When** the user opens /overview, **Then** the user is redirected to /login.

## 10.2 Application shell

### US-SH-001 Global filters

**As a** Executive (CEO/COO/CFO), **I want** to change the reporting period, currency and business unit once in the header, **so that** every figure on the page is calculated for the same context.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story ID | US-SH-001 |
| Screen / component | SCR-00 Application shell / Global filters |
| Persona | Executive (CEO/COO/CFO) |
| Business need | Every figure on the page is calculated for the same context. |
| Preconditions | User is signed in; the dataset passed validation. |
| Main success flow | User changes a header select; the URL updates and the server re-renders the page. |
| Alternate flows | - |
| Error and exception flows | If the CSV dataset fails validation, the page shows 'Dataset unavailable' with the problem list instead of any figure. |
| Business rules | BRL-PER-01, BRL-PER-02, BRL-FX-01, BRL-BU-01 |
| Related KPI IDs | All period KPIs |
| Related chart / table IDs | - |
| Data dependencies | URL parameters range/from/to/cur/bu; dim_fx_rate.csv; dim_client.business_unit |
| Priority | Must |
| Dependencies | - |
| Requirement links | FR-06, BR-03 |
| Implementation status | Implemented |
| Test cases | TC-FIL-01, TC-FIL-02, TC-DATE-01, TC-DATE-02 |

Acceptance criteria:

- **US-SH-001-AC1** — **Given** the user is on Overview, **When** the user selects Trailing 12 months, EUR and Unit Alpha, **Then** the URL becomes ?range=ttm&cur=EUR&bu=UNIT_ALPHA, the period chip reads 2025-10 to 2026-09, money shows €, and KPI cards, charts and tables are recalculated.
- **US-SH-001-AC2** — **Given** the user selects Custom with From 2025-03 and To 2024-06, **When** the page reloads, **Then** the period is 2024-06 to 2025-03 (the values are swapped).
- **US-SH-001-AC3** — **Given** the URL contains an unsupported value such as range=bogus, cur=XXX or bu=ZZZ, **When** the page loads, **Then** it falls back to Year to date, USD and all business units without an error.

# 11. User Journeys

Each journey uses only implemented functionality unless marked. Values are for the default dataset.

## UJ-01 Executive reviews performance and investigates a variance — Implemented

| Step | Screen | Action | What the user sees / decides | KPI / chart IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Login → Overview | Sign in | Ten KPI cards for Year to date; Revenue $1.07M, ▲ +24.6% vs 2025-01..09 | KPI-OV-001…010 |
| 2 | Overview | Hover the Revenue "i" | Definition, formula and source | IE-G-10 |
| 3 | Overview | Open Revenue's Expand analysis | Prior period $860.9K, illustrative target $1.09M, attainment 98.6% (behind), 33-month trend, breakdown by unit, service line, client, tier, vertical | IE-G-11, IE-G-13 |
| 4 | Expand analysis | Drill into a service line | All figures recomputed for that service line | IE-G-14 |
| 5 | Executive Strategy | Open via the sidebar (filters kept) | Revenue vs plan 98.6%, scorecard statuses | KPI-EX-001, KPI-EX-006 |
| 6 | Risk & Alerts | Review critical alerts | 17 critical or high open alerts; read the rule of each | KPI-RA-002, TB-RA-001 |

Expected outcome: the executive can say whether revenue is behind plan, which segment explains the change, and which risks need action.

## UJ-02 Sales manager reviews client revenue and pipeline — Implemented (no client dossier)

1. Client & Revenue: Top-10 concentration 54.8% (KPI-CR-004); top-10 chart (CH-CR-001); health bands (CH-CR-004).
2. Add `?health=AT_RISK` to the URL; the roster (TB-CR-001) lists at-risk clients; open the client-health Expand analysis for at-risk clients sorted by revenue.
3. Sales & Marketing: open pipeline $3.18M, weighted $1.04M, win rate 31.4% (KPI-SM-001…003); loss reasons (CH-SM-003); add `?stage=NEGOTIATION` to list late-stage deals.

Decision: which accounts need retention calls and which deals to push. A client dossier (BRD) is not built (US-CR-005).

## UJ-03 Operations manager investigates delivery and capacity — Implemented

1. Translation Ops: OTD 93.8% (KPI-TR-002); Pipeline status counts (PN-TR-001); add `?lp=EN>UR` to see that pair's active batches.
2. Capacity & Demand: 10 pairs above 100% load in the next 8 weeks; EN>UR load 190% (TB-CD-001); heatmap (CH-CD-002).
3. Interpretation Ops: OPI ASA 38 s; language-pair fill table (TB-IN-001).
4. HR & Workforce: active resources 166, PM utilisation 83.8%; PM workload table (TB-HR-001).

Decision: where to source linguists and how to re-plan deadlines.

## UJ-04 Finance user investigates profitability and receivables — Implemented

1. Finance & Profitability with Year to date: GM 42.1%, EBITDA margin 14.8%, DSO 42.6 days.
2. P&L bridge (TB-FI-001) from revenue to EBITDA; margin by service line (TB-FI-002).
3. AR aging (CH-FI-002) and open receivables by client (TB-FI-003); open the DSO Expand analysis for the clients with the largest overdue balances.
4. Switch currency to EUR: amounts divide by 1.08; margins unchanged.

## UJ-05 Leadership compares baseline and alternative scenarios — Implemented

1. Forecasting & Scenarios: Baseline shows revenue $1.37M, EBITDA $192.1K, margin 14.0%.
2. Select Optimistic: EBITDA $315.4K (+$123.3K), margin 20.0%; Conservative: EBITDA $94.3K.
3. Move Volume growth to +20%: capacity gap changes; the preset label becomes CUSTOM.
4. Open the EBITDA card's expand icon for the line-by-line comparison; Reset returns to Baseline.

Outcome: the trade-offs between AI adoption, price, vendor inflation and volume are explained with a documented formula — not a prediction.

## UJ-06 Data steward investigates a data-quality issue — Implemented

1. A CSV is edited and breaks a rule (for example a duplicate client_id).
2. Within about one second any dashboard shows "Dataset unavailable" with "Duplicate IDs — dim_client: 1 duplicate client_id value(s)…" and examples.
3. The steward fixes the file and presses **Reload data**; dashboards return.
4. Data Governance shows the new SHA-256 prefix and modified time in the CSV inventory and the KPI dictionary for the definitions.

## UJ-07 User submits application feedback — Implemented (local only)

1. Feedback: choose a category, rating 1–5 and a comment (max 500 characters).
2. "Add to local list": the entry appears at the top with "(local only)". A blank comment is ignored without a message (GAP-10).
3. Refreshing the page removes local entries. Nothing is sent to a server.

# 12. Forecasting and Scenario Analysis

## 12.1 What exists

| Element | Implemented method | Not implemented |
|---|---|---|
| Scenario analysis (Forecasting & Scenarios) | Deterministic formula SCN-F1.0 applied in the browser to a trailing-12-month baseline | Any statistical forecast |
| Revenue trajectory ranges | Average monthly TTM revenue grown at fixed annual rates 4%, 11%, 20% for 12 months | Model fitting, intervals |
| Capacity forecast weeks (Capacity & Demand) | Generated by the data generator: average of the last 8 actual weeks × month seasonality (Sep 1.02, Oct 1.06, Nov 1.00, Dec 0.90; 23 Nov 0.90) × 1.0025^week × random 0.95–1.06, plus a +22% seeded surge for AM, SO, HT, VI, ZH in forecast weeks 3–7 (index 2–6). Supply = linguist capacity × availability, reduced in December | Back-testing, accuracy metrics |

None of these is an AI or machine-learning prediction. The UI labels them "illustrative scenario ranges, not statistical forecasts or confidence intervals".

## 12.2 Baseline (historical input)

Trailing 12 months 2025-10 … 2026-09, all business units (scenarioBaseline() in lib/kpi/core.ts):

| Symbol | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Rw, Ri | Written and interpretation revenue | fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd by unit_type |
| W | Written words | Σ units of WORD revenue lines |
| a0 | AI-touched share | MTPE + AIR words ÷ W (= 43.8%) |
| ch, ca | Vendor linguist cost per word for HT and AI-touched work | VENDOR_LINGUIST cost ÷ words |
| t | Tooling cost per AI word | MT_AI_TOOLING ÷ AI words |
| Pi, Pl, L | Interpreter pay, platform/telecom, PM/dispatch labour | fact_cost_line by category |
| X, D | OPEX and D&A | fact_cost_line OPEX / DA of the 12 months |
| S | Average weekly actual linguist supply (words) | fact_capacity_period, is_forecast = false |

## 12.3 Parameters and inputs

| Input | Range in UI | Preset values (fact_scenario_assumption_set.csv) |
|---|---|---|
| AI adoption change (absolute share of words) | −10 … +30 pp, step 1 | Baseline 0; Conservative +3; Optimistic +15 |
| Price change | −10% … +10%, step 0.5 | 0; −2%; +3% |
| Vendor cost inflation | 0 … 20%, step 0.5 | 0; +8%; +2% |
| Volume growth | −20% … +30%, step 1 | 0; −5%; +12% |

Configured parameters (meta_config.csv): AI effort factor 0.35, PM labour volume elasticity 0.6, OPEX volume elasticity 0.25, platform volume elasticity 1.0.

## 12.4 Formulas (SCN-F1.0)

```
W'  = W (1+v)                       a = clamp(a0 + Δa, 0, 1)
Rev' = (Rw + Ri)(1+v)(1+p)
Vendor' = W' [ (1-a) ch + a ca ] (1+i)
Tooling' = W' a t
Interpreter pay' = Pi (1+v)(1+i)
Platform' = Pl (1 + 1.0 v)
Labour' = L (1 + 0.6 v)
GP' = Rev' - Vendor' - Tooling' - Interpreter pay' - Platform' - Labour'      GM' = GP' / Rev'
OPEX' = X (1 + 0.25 v)                EBITDA' = GP' - OPEX'                    EM' = EBITDA' / Rev'
Required human words = W' [ (1-a) + 0.35 a ]        Capacity gap = Required - 52 S   (positive = shortfall)
Trajectory month n = (Σ TTM revenue / 12) (1+r)^(n/12),  r ∈ {0.04, 0.11, 0.20}
```

## 12.5 Outputs and validation

| Output | Baseline | Conservative | Optimistic |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (12 months) | $1.37M | $1.28M | $1.58M |
| Gross margin | 41.6% | 36.7% | 44.6% |
| EBITDA | $192.1K | $94.3K | $315.4K |
| EBITDA margin | 14.0% | 7.4% | 20.0% |
| AI-touched share | 43.8% | 46.8% | 58.8% |
| Capacity gap (words/yr) | −3,303,394 | −3,610,427 | −3,435,659 |

Validation: the TypeScript engine reproduces the Python reference outputs stored in `fact_scenario_output` for all three presets, and the Baseline EBITDA equals trailing-12-month EBITDA from core() (TC-SCN-01, executed 25 Oct 2026). Identical inputs always give identical outputs.

## 12.6 How results are compared and presented

Each result card shows the scenario value and its difference from the Baseline preset (relative % for revenue, percentage points for margins, money difference for EBITDA). The grouped bar chart compares five P&L lines; each card's expand view lists 13 lines side by side. A notice states that calculations run in the browser, nothing is saved, and results are illustrative. Uncertainty is not quantified; the spread between presets is the only "range" (FORECAST_RANGE).

## 12.7 Acceptance criteria

- Changing an input recalculates only outputs that depend on it, without a page reload (US-FS-001).
- Baseline reproduces TTM EBITDA within rounding (TC-SCN-01).
- No text calls a range a "confidence interval" or a prediction (BRL-SCN-02).

# 13. Authentication, Security and Data Governance

## 13.1 Login and logout flow

1. Unauthenticated request to any protected path → `proxy.ts` redirects (307) to `/login` and deletes an invalid cookie.
2. `/login` form submits to the `login` server action. If `DEMO_USERNAME`, `DEMO_PASSWORD` or a `SESSION_SECRET` of at least 32 characters is missing → "Sign-in is not configured on this server."
3. Inputs are truncated to 200 characters and compared with the environment values as SHA-256 digests using `timingSafeEqual`; both fields are always evaluated.
4. Failure → "Invalid username or password." (username kept). Success → signed token in cookie `bls_oneview_session` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Secure when NODE_ENV=production, max-age 8 h) and redirect to `/overview`.
5. A signed-in user who opens `/login` is redirected to `/overview`.
6. Sign out → `logout` server action deletes the cookie and redirects to `/login`.

## 13.2 Session handling

Token = base64url(JSON {sub, iat, exp}) + "." + base64url(HMAC-SHA256(secret, payload)), verified with Web Crypto (constant-time) in the proxy, the dashboard layout and both API routes. Expired, malformed or wrongly signed tokens are rejected. Tokens are stateless: they cannot be revoked individually before expiry; rotating `SESSION_SECRET` invalidates all sessions.

## 13.3 Environment variables

| Variable | Purpose | Required |
|---|---|---|
| DEMO_USERNAME | Demo account name (`Demo_project_for_interview`) | Yes |
| DEMO_PASSWORD | Private password — never committed; written locally by `npm run setup:env` | Yes |
| SESSION_SECRET | ≥ 32 random characters for signing | Yes |
| DATA_DIR | Optional alternative folder for the CSV files | No |

`.env*` files are git-ignored except `.env.example` (placeholders only). This document contains no password, secret or token.

## 13.4 Protected routes and input validation

Protected: every path except `/login`, `/_next/static`, `/_next/image`, `favicon.ico` and image files — including `/data/*.csv` downloads, `/api/analysis` and `/api/data` (which also return 401 themselves). URL filters are validated against allow-lists; unknown values fall back to defaults. `/api/analysis` accepts only known keys and valid drill segments (404 otherwise). Feedback input is limited to 500 characters and rendered as text.

## 13.5 Error messages

Generic login errors; "Dataset unavailable" lists data problems (no stack traces); the error boundary shows a reference digest only; the analysis dialog shows "Your session has expired…" or "The analysis could not be loaded (HTTP n)".

## 13.6 Data classification and synthetic labelling

All tables are classified SYNTHETIC_* in the data dictionary (identifier, financial, operational, workforce-sensitive). Names are fictional; linguists and owners appear only as anonymised codes (L-0001, I-0001, PM-01). Disclosure: header badge, Expand analysis badge and closing insight, page notes, info texts, the meta_dataset disclaimer ("All records are synthetic and fictional. Nothing here is BIG Language Solutions data."), simulated-connector banner and `.invalid` endpoints.

## 13.7 Auditability and logging

No application logging of credentials or user actions; no audit trail. Data provenance is auditable through the CSV inventory (row counts, sizes, SHA-256, modified time), the dataset version and seed, and 864 recorded validation checks.

## 13.8 Accessibility

Semantic landmarks, visible focus rings, labelled controls, keyboard-operable info popovers and dialogs with focus management, aria-sort on tables, text status (not colour alone), and data-table alternatives for charts in the expanded view. Not formally audited (TC-NF-02 not executed). Known gaps: alert rows are mouse-only (GAP-03); the mobile drawer has no focus trap.

## 13.9 Limitations of the demo security model

Single shared account; no MFA, SSO, roles or per-user audit; no login rate limiting (GAP-06); stateless sessions; deployment not performed. Not production identity and not a security certification.

## 16.3 Definition of done — per screen

A screen is done when: (1) every KPI, chart and table listed for it in Sections 5–6 renders from the shared KPI layer for the URL filters; (2) each has an info icon whose text matches Section 5/Appendix L; (3) components that claim to reconcile do so (Section 4 point 9); (4) loading, invalid-data and empty states behave as in Section 4 point 10; (5) its user stories' acceptance criteria pass; (6) its open GAP entries are fixed or explicitly accepted; (7) the synthetic badge is visible.

## 16.4 Definition of done — application

- All 18 routes and /login render; unauthenticated access redirects (TC-UI-01, TC-AUTH-01) — evidence 2026-10-23.

# Appendix B — KPI Dictionary (canonical, dim_kpi_definition.csv)

All 81 canonical definitions with the displayed KPIs that use them. 'Not displayed' = defined (and in several cases computed) but not shown on any screen.

| ID | Name | Domain | Definition | Formula | Unit | Direction | Illustrative target | Displayed as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REV | Recognized revenue | Finance | Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. Not bookings, invoices or cash. | SUM(revenue_usd) over revenue lines in range, converted to reporting currency | USD (or EUR/GBP) | Higher | Plan = smoothed trend +3% (fact_kpi_target_period) | KPI-OV-001, KPI-CR-001, KPI-FI-001 |
| REV_VS_PLAN | Revenue vs plan (variance) | Finance | Actual recognised revenue minus the illustrative plan for the same months; variance % = variance / plan. | (REV - SUM(target REVENUE_USD)) ; variance % = (REV - plan) / plan | USD / % | Higher | 0% or better | Not displayed |
| DIRECT_COST | Direct costs | Finance | Costs directly attributed to delivering revenue: vendor linguists, interpreter pay, MT/AI tooling, platform/telecom, project-management and dispatch labour allocation. | SUM(amount_usd) where cost_class = DIRECT | USD | Lower | n/a | KPI-FI-006 |
| GP | Gross profit | Finance | Recognised revenue less direct costs (categories listed in DIRECT_COST). Operating expenses and D&A are excluded. | GP = REV - DIRECT_COST | USD | Higher | - | KPI-FI-002 |
| GM | Gross margin | Finance | Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. | GM = GP / REV | Fraction (shown %) | Higher | >= 38% | KPI-OV-002, KPI-EX-002, KPI-FI-003 |
| OPEX | Operating expenses | Finance | Sales & marketing, technology & product, and general & admin expenses. Excludes direct costs and D&A. | SUM(amount_usd) where cost_class = OPEX | USD | Lower | - | KPI-FI-007 |
| EBITDA | EBITDA | Finance | Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation = gross profit less operating expenses. D&A is shown separately below EBITDA in the bridge; interest and tax are out of scope. | EBITDA = GP - OPEX | USD | Higher | - | KPI-EX-003, KPI-FI-008 |
| EBITDA_M | EBITDA margin | Finance | EBITDA / recognised revenue. | EBITDA_M = EBITDA / REV | Fraction | Higher | >= 12% | KPI-OV-003, KPI-FI-004 |
| VENDOR_COGS_SHARE | Vendor COGS share | Finance | Third-party linguist and interpreter pay as a share of revenue. | (VENDOR_LINGUIST + INTERPRETER_PAY) / REV | Fraction | Lower | <= 52% | Not displayed |
| COST_PER_WORD | Vendor cost per word | Finance | Vendor linguist cost per delivered written word (same delivered-batch population as revenue per word). | SUM(VENDOR_LINGUIST) / SUM(words) for written revenue lines | USD per word | Lower | - | Not displayed |
| REV_PER_WORD | Revenue per word | Finance | Written recognised revenue per delivered word. | SUM(revenue_usd written) / SUM(units written) | USD per word | Higher | - | Not displayed |
| DSO | Days sales outstanding (demo formula) | Finance | Simplified demo DSO: open receivables at the range end divided by invoiced value in the trailing 90 days, times 90. Receivable = invoiced less allocated cash receipts received on or before the range end. | DSO = open_AR_usd(end) / invoiced_usd(end-89d..end) * 90 | Days | Lower | <= 50 days | KPI-OV-010, KPI-FI-005 |
| ACTIVE_CLIENTS | Active clients | Clients | Clients with recognised revenue > 0 in the selected range. | COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) with revenue_usd > 0 in range | Count | Higher | - | KPI-OV-004, KPI-CR-002 |
| ARPA | Average revenue per account | Clients | Revenue divided by active clients in the same range. | ARPA = REV / ACTIVE_CLIENTS | USD | Higher | - | KPI-CR-003 |
| TOP10_CONC | Top-10 client concentration | Clients | Share of revenue from the ten largest clients in the range. | SUM(revenue of top 10 clients) / REV | Fraction | Lower | <= 55% | KPI-CR-004 |
| NRR | Net revenue retention | Clients | Fixed opening cohort = clients with revenue in the 12 months ending 12 months before the range end. NRR = cohort revenue in the latest 12 months / cohort revenue in the opening 12 months. New clients are excluded; expansion and contraction included. | NRR = SUM(cohort revenue, latest 12m) / SUM(cohort revenue, opening 12m) | Fraction | Higher | >= 100% | KPI-OV-005, KPI-CR-005 |
| GROSS_REV_CHURN | Gross revenue churn | Clients | Revenue-based gross churn for the NRR cohort: revenue lost from churn and contraction, ignoring expansion. | SUM(max(0, opening_i - latest_i)) / SUM(opening_i) | Fraction | Lower | <= 8% | KPI-CR-006 |
| LOGO_CHURN | Logo churn | Clients | Share of NRR-cohort clients with zero revenue in the latest 12 months. | COUNT(cohort clients with latest_i = 0) / COUNT(cohort) | Fraction | Lower | <= 10% | Not displayed |
| LOGO_RETENTION | Client retention (logo) | Clients | 1 - logo churn over the same cohort and window. | 1 - LOGO_CHURN | Fraction | Higher | >= 90% | KPI-CR-007 |

Bands: healthy >= 0.70, watch >= 0.50, else at risk. | See formula; latest snapshot at or before range end | Fraction | Higher | >= 0.70 | KPI-CR-009 |
| PIPE_UNW | Pipeline value (unweighted) | Sales | Sum of estimated annual contract value of open opportunities (stage not closed) at range end. | SUM(value_usd) for opportunities open at range end | USD | Higher | - | KPI-SM-001 |
| PIPE_W | Pipeline value (weighted) | Sales | Open pipeline weighted by stage probability. | SUM(value_usd * probability) | USD | Higher | - | KPI-SM-002 |
| WIN_RATE_COUNT | Win rate (by count) | Sales | Closed-won opportunities / (closed-won + closed-lost) closed in the range. | won_count / (won_count + lost_count) | Fraction | Higher | >= 25% | KPI-SM-003 |
| WIN_RATE_VALUE | Win rate (by value) | Sales | Closed-won value / (closed-won + closed-lost value). Reported separately from count win rate. | won_value / (won_value + lost_value) | Fraction | Higher | - | Not displayed |
| SALES_CYCLE | Sales cycle length | Sales | Average days from creation to close for closed-won opportunities. | AVG(closed_date - created_date) for won | Days | Lower | - | Not displayed |
| QUOTE_TAT | Quote turnaround | Sales | Average hours from quote request to quote issued. | AVG(quote_turnaround_hours) | Hours | Lower | <= 24 h | KPI-SM-005 |
| MQL | Marketing-qualified leads | Sales | Opportunities that entered the QUALIFIED stage during the month. | COUNT(stage events where stage = QUALIFIED) | Count | Higher | - | Not displayed |
| CAC | Customer acquisition cost (blended) | Sales | Blended CAC = sales & marketing operating expense in the range divided by new-logo clients onboarded in the range. Attribution is blended (not channel-level). | SALES_MARKETING OPEX / COUNT(clients with onboarding_date in range) | USD | Lower | - | Not displayed |

| TR_TAT | Average turnaround time | Translation | Mean calendar days from batch start to delivery for delivered batches. | AVG(delivered_date - start_date) | Days | Lower | - | KPI-TR-003 |
| TR_OTD | Translation on-time delivery | Translation | Delivered batches with delivered_date <= due_date divided by all delivered batches in the range. | on_time_batches / delivered_batches | Fraction | Higher | >= 95% | KPI-OV-006, KPI-TR-002 |
| MTPE_SHARE | MTPE word share | Translation | Words in workflow MTPE divided by all delivered written words in the same range and population as TR_WORDS. | SUM(words \| workflow = MTPE) / TR_WORDS | Fraction | Higher (adoption) | - | Not displayed |
| TM_REUSE | Translation-memory reuse | Translation | Words covered by TM matches divided by delivered words in the same population. | SUM(tm_match_words) / TR_WORDS | Fraction | Higher | - | KPI-TR-004 |
| ACTIVE_PROJECTS | Active projects | Translation | Projects started on or before the range end and not delivered by that date. | COUNT(projects with start <= end and (delivered is null or delivered > end)) | Count | n/a | - | Not displayed |

# Appendix E — Business Glossary

| Term | Meaning in this application |
|---|---|
| AIR | AI-assisted review: machine output with a light linguist review (workflow). |
| AI-touched | Words produced in MTPE or AIR workflows. |
| ARPA | Average revenue per active client. |
| ASA | Average speed to answer: seconds to connect an interpreter (fulfilled on-demand OPI). |
| Bookings | Estimated annual contract value of won opportunities; not revenue. |
| CAC | Customer acquisition cost (defined in the dictionary, not shown). |
| COMET / BLEU | Translation evaluation metrics; not used and never mixed with QE or edit distance. |
| Cut-off | 2026-09-30, the last day of the synthetic data. |
| D&A | Depreciation and amortisation. |
| DSO | Days sales outstanding (demo formula, BRL-AR-02). |
| EBITDA | Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation = gross profit − operating expenses. |
| Edit distance | Share of a machine translation changed in post-editing (0 = none, 1 = rewritten). |
| Fill rate | Fulfilled ÷ (fulfilled + unfulfilled) requests. |
| GM | Gross margin = (revenue − direct costs) ÷ revenue. |
| HT | Human translation workflow. |
| LQA / MQM | Language quality assessment / multidimensional quality metrics; the app uses one illustrative MQM-style score. |
| MTPE | Machine translation post-editing (workflow, not a service line). |
| MTQE | Machine-translation quality estimation; acceptance threshold 0.85. |
| NRR | Net revenue retention of a fixed opening cohort. |
| OPEX | Operating expenses: sales & marketing, technology & product, general & admin. |
| OPI / VRI / On-site | Over-the-phone, video remote and on-site interpretation service lines. |
| OTD | On-time delivery. |
| pp | Percentage points. |
| Prior period | Comparison window (BRL-PER-02). |
| Service line | Mutually exclusive revenue category (6). |
| SLA | Service-level agreement (due dates). |
| Synthetic data | Generated, fictional records; not BLS data. |
| TAT | Turnaround time in calendar days. |
| TM | Translation memory; TM reuse = matched words ÷ words. |
| TTM / YTD / QTD | Trailing 12 months / year to date / quarter to date (whole months). |
| Unit | Fictional business unit Alpha, Beta or Gamma (dim_client.business_unit). |

# Appendix G — Formula Reference

| Displayed KPI | Label | Formula as implemented | Canonical formula (dictionary) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI-OV-001 | Revenue | REV = Σ fact_revenue_line.revenue_usd for lines with month_id in the selected months and client in the selected unit; displayed = REV ÷ fx(cur) | SUM(revenue_usd) over revenue lines in range, converted to reporting currency |
| KPI-OV-002 | Gross margin | GM = (REV − DIRECT) ÷ REV, where DIRECT = Σ fact_cost_line.amount_usd with cost_class = DIRECT attached (revenue_id) to the in-scope revenue lines | GM = GP / REV |
| KPI-OV-003 | EBITDA margin | EBITDA_M = (GP − OPEX_alloc) ÷ REV; OPEX_alloc = Σ OPEX of the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV) | EBITDA_M = EBITDA / REV |
| KPI-OV-004 | Active clients | COUNT DISTINCT client_id whose Σ revenue_usd in the selected months > 0 | COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) with revenue_usd > 0 in range |
| KPI-OV-005 | Net revenue retention (TTM) | Cohort = clients with revenue > 0 in 2024-10..2025-09; NRR = Σ cohort revenue 2025-10..2026-09 ÷ Σ cohort revenue 2024-10..2025-09 | NRR = SUM(cohort revenue, latest 12m) / SUM(cohort revenue, opening 12m) |
| KPI-OV-006 | Translation on-time delivery | TR_OTD = COUNT(delivered batches with delivered_date ≤ due_date) ÷ COUNT(delivered batches), delivered in the selected months | on_time_batches / delivered_batches |
| KPI-OV-007 | OPI speed to answer | OPI_ASA = mean(connect_seconds) over sessions with service_line_id = OPI, request_type = ON_DEMAND, status = FULFILLED | AVG(connect_seconds \| OPI, ON_DEMAND, FULFILLED) |
| KPI-OV-008 | AI-touched word share | AI_SHARE = Σ words_total (workflow_id ≠ HT) ÷ Σ words_total, delivered batches in the selected months | SUM(words \| workflow in MTPE, AIR) / TR_WORDS |
| KPI-OV-009 | Quality score | QUALITY_SCORE = mean(fact_quality_evaluation.score) for evaluations in the selected months; score = max(0, 100 − (minor×1 + major×5 + critical×25) × 1000 ÷ sample_words) | AVG(score) |
| KPI-OV-010 | DSO (days) | DSO = Σ open_usd ÷ Σ amount_usd of invoices dated 2026-07-03..2026-09-30 (last 90 days) × 90; open_usd = amount_usd − Σ allocations paid on or before 2026-09-30 | DSO = open_AR_usd(end) / invoiced_usd(end-89d..end) * 90 |
| KPI-EX-001 | Revenue vs plan | Attainment = REV ÷ PLAN; PLAN = Σ fact_kpi_target_period.target_value (kpi_id = REV) over the selected months × (unit REV ÷ company REV when a unit is selected) | - |
| KPI-EX-002 | Gross margin | Same as KPI-OV-002 | GM = GP / REV |
| KPI-EX-003 | EBITDA | EBITDA = GP − OPEX_alloc (see KPI-OV-003); displayed ÷ fx(cur) | EBITDA = GP - OPEX |
| KPI-EX-004 | OKRs on track or complete | COUNT(fact_okr.status ∈ {ON_TRACK, COMPLETE}) ÷ COUNT(fact_okr) | - |
| KPI-EX-005 | OKR progress by pillar | mean(fact_okr.progress) per pillar; progress = clamp((current − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline), 0, 1) | AVG(progress) |
| KPI-EX-006 | Scorecard attainment (6 KPIs) | Attainment = actual ÷ target; REV target = Σ monthly plan (scaled by unit share); GM, EBITDA_M, TR_OTD, FILL_ON_DEMAND, QUALITY_SCORE targets = mean of monthly targets. Status: On target ≥ 100%, Near ≥ 97%, else Behind | - |
| KPI-EX-007 | Monthly revenue plan | Plan(m) = fact_kpi_target_period.target_value (REV, month m) × (unit share of revenue over the selected period); generated as a centred 5-month rolling mean of actual revenue × 1.03 | - |
| KPI-CR-001 | Revenue | Same as KPI-OV-001 | SUM(revenue_usd) over revenue lines in range, converted to reporting currency |
| KPI-CR-002 | Active clients | Same as KPI-OV-004 | COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) with revenue_usd > 0 in range |
| KPI-CR-003 | Revenue per active client | ARPA = REV ÷ ACTIVE_CLIENTS | ARPA = REV / ACTIVE_CLIENTS |
| KPI-CR-004 | Top-10 concentration | TOP10_CONC = Σ revenue of the 10 largest clients (by period revenue) ÷ REV | SUM(revenue of top 10 clients) / REV |
| KPI-CR-005 | Net revenue retention | Same as KPI-OV-005 | NRR = SUM(cohort revenue, latest 12m) / SUM(cohort revenue, opening 12m) |
| KPI-CR-006 | Gross revenue churn | Σ max(0, opening_i − latest_i) ÷ Σ opening_i over the NRR cohort | SUM(max(0, opening_i - latest_i)) / SUM(opening_i) |
| KPI-CR-007 | Logo retention | 1 − COUNT(cohort clients with latest-12-month revenue ≤ 0) ÷ COUNT(cohort) | 1 - LOGO_CHURN |
| KPI-CR-008 | Cohort size | COUNT(clients with opening-window revenue > 0) | - |
| KPI-CR-009 | Client health score and band | health = Σ wᵢ·cᵢ ÷ Σ wᵢ over available components (0.30 otd_90d, 0.25 quality_norm, 0.20 payment_timeliness, 0.25 revenue_trend_norm); band HEALTHY ≥ 0.70, WATCH ≥ 0.50, else AT_RISK. Read from the 2026-09 snapshot | See formula; latest snapshot at or before range end |
| KPI-SM-001 | Open pipeline | Σ value_usd for opportunities with closed_date empty (open at the cut-off) | SUM(value_usd) for opportunities open at range end |
| KPI-SM-002 | Weighted pipeline | Σ value_usd × probability over open opportunities | SUM(value_usd * probability) |
| KPI-SM-003 | Win rate (closed in period) | COUNT(stage_current = CLOSED_WON) ÷ COUNT(closed_date in period), where closed = CLOSED_WON or CLOSED_LOST | won_count / (won_count + lost_count) |
| KPI-SM-004 | Won value | Σ value_usd for CLOSED_WON opportunities with closed_date in period | - |
| KPI-SM-005 | Avg quote turnaround (h) | mean(quote_turnaround_hours) for opportunities with created_date in period (nulls ignored) | AVG(quote_turnaround_hours) |
| KPI-SM-006 | Funnel stage reach | For each stage in LEAD, QUALIFIED, PROPOSAL, NEGOTIATION, CLOSED_WON: COUNT DISTINCT opportunity_id with a stage event for that stage, among opportunities created in the period | - |
| KPI-SM-007 | Win rate by lead source | Per lead_source: COUNT(CLOSED_WON) ÷ COUNT(closed in period) | - |
| KPI-SM-008 | Loss reasons | COUNT of CLOSED_LOST opportunities closed in period, per loss_reason (empty → UNSPECIFIED) | - |
| KPI-TR-001 | Words delivered | TR_WORDS = Σ words_total for batches with status = DELIVERED and delivered month in the selected months | SUM(words_total) for delivered batches |
| KPI-TR-002 | On-time delivery | Same as KPI-OV-006 | on_time_batches / delivered_batches |
| KPI-TR-003 | Turnaround (days) | TR_TAT = mean((delivered_date − start_date) in days) over delivered batches | AVG(delivered_date - start_date) |
| KPI-TR-004 | Translation-memory reuse | TM_REUSE = Σ tm_match_words ÷ Σ words_total, delivered batches | SUM(tm_match_words) / TR_WORDS |
| KPI-TR-005 | Client rejection rate | REJECTION_RATE = COUNT(client_rejected = true) ÷ COUNT(delivered batches) | SUM(client_rejected) / delivered batches |
| KPI-TR-006 | Pipeline status counts (On track / At risk / Overdue) | For batches with status ≠ DELIVERED: Overdue if due_date < 2026-09-30; At risk if (due_date − 2026-09-30) ≤ 2 days and pct_complete < 0.8; otherwise On track (slaStatus in lib/kpi/rules.ts) | COUNT(batches overdue or (due - as_of <= 2 and pct_complete < 0.8)) |
| KPI-TR-007 | Language-pair performance (batches, words, on-time, turnaround, AI share) | Per lp_id over delivered batches in period: COUNT, Σ words_total, on-time ratio, mean turnaround, Σ words (workflow ≠ HT) ÷ Σ words | - |
| KPI-IN-001 | Interpreted minutes | INT_MIN = Σ duration_min for sessions with status = FULFILLED, requested in the selected months | SUM(duration_min) where status = FULFILLED |
| KPI-IN-002 | OPI speed to answer | Same as KPI-OV-007 | AVG(connect_seconds \| OPI, ON_DEMAND, FULFILLED) |
| KPI-IN-003 | On-demand fill rate | FILL_ON_DEMAND = COUNT(FULFILLED) ÷ (COUNT(FULFILLED) + COUNT(UNFULFILLED)) for request_type = ON_DEMAND (cancellations and technical failures excluded) | FULFILLED / (FULFILLED + UNFULFILLED) for ON_DEMAND |
| KPI-IN-004 | VRI connection success | VRI_CONN = COUNT(VRI FULFILLED) ÷ (COUNT(VRI FULFILLED) + COUNT(VRI TECH_FAILURE)) | FULFILLED / (FULFILLED + TECH_FAILURE) for VRI |
| KPI-IN-005 | Avg session length (min) | INT_AVG_DUR = mean(duration_min) over FULFILLED sessions | AVG(duration_min \| FULFILLED) |
| KPI-IN-006 | Language-pair fill rate and OPI ASA (table) | Per lp_id over sessions in period: requests = COUNT; minutes = Σ duration_min (FULFILLED); fill = FULFILLED ÷ max(1, FULFILLED + UNFULFILLED) across all request types; ASA = mean connect_seconds of fulfilled on-demand OPI | - |
| KPI-IN-007 | Requests by hour | COUNT(sessions, any status) per request_hour 0–23 in the selected months | - |
| KPI-QC-001 | Quality score | Same as KPI-OV-009 | AVG(score) |
| KPI-QC-002 | Review pass rate | REVIEW_PASS = COUNT(outcome = PASS) ÷ COUNT(evaluations); PASS when score ≥ 90 and critical_count = 0 | PASS / evaluations |
| KPI-QC-003 | Errors per 1,000 words | Σ(critical_count + major_count + minor_count) ÷ max(1, Σ sample_words) × 1000, evaluations in period (not severity-weighted) | - |
| KPI-QC-004 | Open disputes | COUNT(evaluations in period with dispute_status = OPEN) | COUNT(dispute_status = OPEN) |
| KPI-QC-005 | Open corrective actions | COUNT(evaluations in period with corrective_status = OPEN and corrective_action ≠ NONE_REQUIRED) | - |
| KPI-QC-006 | Errors by category and severity | COUNT(fact_quality_error) per category × severity for errors of evaluations in period | - |
| KPI-HR-001 | Active resources | COUNT(dim_resource.is_active = true) | COUNT(resources active) |
| KPI-HR-002 | Avg quality score (active) | mean(dim_resource.quality_score) over active resources | - |
| KPI-HR-003 | Avg onboarding time (days) | mean(onboarded_date − application_date) in days over all resources with an onboarded_date | AVG(onboarded_date - application_date) |
| KPI-HR-004 | PM utilisation | PM_UTIL = Σ est_pm_hours × (days of the project inside the window ÷ project span days) ÷ Σ weekly_capacity_hours × (days employed in the window ÷ 7), project managers only | SUM(est_pm_hours allocated to range) / SUM(weekly_capacity_hours x weeks) |
| KPI-HR-005 | PM workload (per PM) | Per PM: allocated hours as above for that PM's projects; capacity = weekly_capacity_hours × days employed ÷ 7; utilisation = allocated ÷ capacity. Window ends on day 28 of the last month | - |
| KPI-CD-001 | Forecast load, next 8 weeks | Σ demand_words ÷ Σ supply_words over the first 8 forecast weeks (all pairs, or the ?lp= pair) | SUM(demand_words) / SUM(supply_words) |
| KPI-CD-002 | Pairs with a shortfall | COUNT(language pairs with Σ demand ÷ Σ supply > 1.0 over the first 8 forecast weeks) | - |
| KPI-CD-003 | Largest gap (words, 8 wks) | max(0, demand − supply) of the first row of the shortfall list sorted by load (highest load), i.e. the gap of the highest-load pair | - |
| KPI-CD-004 | Forecast weeks | COUNT DISTINCT week_start with is_forecast = true | - |
| KPI-CD-005 | Pair load and status (table) | Per pair over the first 8 forecast weeks: load = Σ demand ÷ Σ supply; gap = max(0, Σ demand − Σ supply); status Shortfall > 1.0, Tight > 0.90, else OK | SUM(demand_words) / SUM(supply_words) |
| KPI-FI-001 | Revenue | Same as KPI-OV-001 | SUM(revenue_usd) over revenue lines in range, converted to reporting currency |
| KPI-FI-002 | Gross profit | GP = REV − DIRECT; displayed ÷ fx(cur) | GP = REV - DIRECT_COST |
| KPI-FI-003 | Gross margin | Same as KPI-OV-002 | GM = GP / REV |
| KPI-FI-004 | EBITDA margin | Same as KPI-OV-003 | EBITDA_M = EBITDA / REV |
| KPI-FI-005 | DSO (days) | Same as KPI-OV-010 | DSO = open_AR_usd(end) / invoiced_usd(end-89d..end) * 90 |
| KPI-FI-006 | Direct cost lines (P&L) | Per direct category (VENDOR_LINGUIST, INTERPRETER_PAY, MT_AI_TOOLING, PLATFORM_TELECOM, PM_DISPATCH_LABOR): −Σ amount_usd of direct costs attached to in-scope revenue lines; % of revenue = line ÷ REV | SUM(amount_usd) where cost_class = DIRECT |
| KPI-FI-007 | Operating expense lines (P&L) | Per OPEX category (SALES_MARKETING, TECHNOLOGY_PRODUCT, GENERAL_ADMIN): −Σ OPEX amount_usd of the selected months × (OPEX_alloc ÷ total OPEX) | SUM(amount_usd) where cost_class = OPEX |
| KPI-FI-008 | EBITDA (P&L line) | Same as KPI-EX-003 | EBITDA = GP - OPEX |
| KPI-FI-009 | Margin by service line | Per service_line_id: revenue = Σ revenue_usd; direct = Σ direct cost; gross margin = (revenue − direct) ÷ revenue | - |
| KPI-FI-010 | Receivables aging | Open balances (> $1) grouped by days past due at the cut-off: not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ | - |
| KPI-FI-011 | Open and overdue receivables by client | Per client: open = Σ open_usd (> $1); overdue = Σ open_usd for invoices with due_date < 2026-09-30 | - |
| KPI-AI-001 | AI-touched word share | Same as KPI-OV-008 | SUM(words \| workflow in MTPE, AIR) / TR_WORDS |
| KPI-AI-002 | MTQE acceptance | MTQE_ACCEPT = Σ mtqe_accepted_words ÷ Σ words_total over AI batches delivered in period (segment QE ≥ 0.85) | SUM(mtqe_accepted_words) / SUM(AI words) |
| KPI-AI-003 | Edit distance (words-weighted) | AI_EDIT_DIST = Σ(edit_distance × words_total) ÷ Σ words_total | SUM(edit_distance x words) / SUM(words) |
| KPI-AI-004 | Estimated hours saved | Σ est_hours_saved; per batch = words ÷ 380 − words ÷ observed_words_per_hour | SUM(est_hours_saved) |
| KPI-AI-005 | Estimated cost saved | Σ est_cost_saved_usd; per batch = hours saved × $32 − tooling cost; displayed ÷ fx(cur) | SUM(est_cost_saved_usd) |
| KPI-AI-006 | Engine category metrics (table) | Per engine_category: batches; words; avg QE = Σ(mtqe_score × words) ÷ Σ words; accepted = Σ accepted ÷ Σ words; edit = Σ(edit × words) ÷ Σ words; saved = Σ est_cost_saved_usd ÷ fx | - |
| KPI-AI-007 | Content sensitivity mix | Per content_sensitivity: Σ words_total ÷ Σ words_total of all AI batches in period | - |
| KPI-TE-001 | Overall uptime (90 d) | Σ up_minutes ÷ Σ monitored_minutes over all connector-days | SUM(up_minutes) / SUM(monitored_minutes) |
| KPI-TE-002 | Error rate | Σ(errors_4xx + errors_5xx + errors_timeout) ÷ Σ requests | SUM(errors) / SUM(requests) |
| KPI-TE-003 | Avg p95 latency (ms) | Simple mean of p95_ms across all connector-days | SUM(p95_ms x requests) / SUM(requests) |
| KPI-TE-004 | Degraded connectors | COUNT(connectors with Σ up ÷ Σ monitored over 90 days < 0.995) | - |
| KPI-TE-005 | Connector health (table) | Per connector: uptime, Σ requests, error rate, Σ records_ingested (INGEST_VOL), mean p95, mean p99; status Degraded if uptime < 0.995 | - |
| KPI-TE-006 | Error mix | Σ errors_4xx, Σ errors_5xx, Σ errors_timeout over 90 days | - |
| KPI-RA-001 | Open alerts | COUNT(fact_risk_alert.status ≠ RESOLVED) | COUNT(status in OPEN, IN_PROGRESS) |
| KPI-RA-002 | Critical + high | COUNT(open alerts with severity ∈ {CRITICAL, HIGH}) | - |
| KPI-RA-003 | Exposure (USD, indicative) | Σ exposure_usd over open alerts | - |
| KPI-RA-004 | Resolved | COUNT(all alerts) − COUNT(open alerts) | - |
| KPI-RA-005 | Risk matrix cell count | COUNT(open alerts) per likelihood (1–5) × impact (1–5) | - |
| KPI-FS-001 | Revenue (12 months) | Rev′ = (Rw + Ri) × (1 + volume) × (1 + price) | Rev' = Rev x (1+v) x (1+p) |
| KPI-FS-002 | Gross margin | GM′ = GP′ ÷ Rev′; GP′ = Rev′ − vendor′ − tooling′ − interpreter pay′ − platform′ − labour′ | see docs/architecture.md section Scenario formulas |
| KPI-FS-003 | EBITDA | EBITDA′ = GP′ − OPEX × (1 + 0.25 × volume) | EBITDA' - EBITDA |
| KPI-FS-004 | EBITDA margin | EM′ = EBITDA′ ÷ Rev′ | - |
| KPI-FS-005 | AI-touched word share | a = clamp(a0 + AI adoption change, 0, 1); a0 = MTPE + AIR words ÷ all written words on trailing-12-month revenue lines | - |
| KPI-FS-006 | Capacity gap (words/yr) | Gap = W′ × ((1 − a) + 0.35 × a) − 52 × S; S = mean weekly actual supply_words (sum over pairs) | Required - Supply |
| KPI-FS-007 | Revenue trajectory ranges | Month n (1..12) = avg monthly revenue of the last 12 months × (1 + r)^(n ÷ 12) ÷ fx, for r = 4% (conservative), 11% (target), 20% (aggressive) from meta_config.csv | min/max across presets |
| KPI-DG-001 | Validation checks passed | COUNT(fact_data_quality_check.passed = true) ÷ COUNT(checks) | passed checks / total checks |
| KPI-DG-002 | Tables | COUNT(data files in the loader report, metadata files excluded) | - |
| KPI-DG-003 | Rows (all tables) | Σ valid rows loaded per data table | - |
| KPI-DG-004 | KPI definitions | COUNT(dim_kpi_definition) | - |
| KPI-DG-005 | Dataset size (MB) | Σ bytes of data CSV files ÷ 1,048,576 | - |
| KPI-DG-006 | Validation pass rate by dimension | Per dimension (COMPLETENESS, UNIQUENESS, VALIDITY, CONSISTENCY, INTEGRITY, RECONCILIATION): passed ÷ checks | - |

Scenario formulas: Section 12.4. Business-rule formulas: Section 8.

# Appendix K — Source Document References

See Section 1.4 (SRC-01…09). Code references use repository-relative paths, for example `lib/kpi/core.ts` (KPI layer), `lib/analysis/engine.ts` (Expand analysis), `lib/info/registry.ts` (info texts), `components/DataTable.tsx`, `proxy.ts`.

# Appendix L — Information Icon Texts (verbatim from the application)

Captured on 25 Oct 2026 by calling the application's info registry (`X(key)`, `K(id)`, `lib/info/global.ts`). Page-level overrides are described in Section 7.2.

**`ai.assumptions`** — Title: Assumptions behind the savings estimate. Summary: The fixed inputs that drive every hours-saved and cost-saved figure on this tab. How it is calculated: Assumptions: human baseline 380 words/hour, review cost $32/hour, full post-edit 600 w/h, light review 2000 w/h, tooling $0.004 per AI word. QE acceptance threshold 0.85. Data source: assumptions.* in public/data/meta_config.csv. Caveats: Changing any assumption changes the estimates proportionally; they are not editable in this demo. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from public/data/meta_config.csv (code).

**`ai.batches`** — Title: Largest estimated savings. Summary: The 500 AI-touched batches with the highest estimated cost saving in the period. How it is calculated: Sorted by est_cost_saved_usd, top 500. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Savings are estimates from the documented assumptions. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/ai-automation/page.tsx (code).

**`ai.engine`** — Title: By engine category. Summary: AI-touched batches grouped by generic engine category, with quality and savings indicators. How it is calculated: Avg QE score and edit distance are word-weighted means. Accepted = words with segment QE ≥ 0.85 ÷ words. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Engine categories are generic and synthetic, not vendors. Quality uses QE score and edit distance only; BLEU and COMET are not used. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/ai-automation/page.tsx (code).

**`ai.savings`** — Title: Estimated savings by month. Summary: Estimated net cost impact of AI-touched batches, by delivery month. How it is calculated: Sum of est_cost_saved_usd = hours saved × review hourly cost − tooling cost. Hours saved = words ÷ baseline words per hour − words ÷ observed words per hour. Assumptions: human baseline 380 words/hour, review cost $32/hour, full post-edit 600 w/h, light review 2000 w/h, tooling $0.004 per AI word. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: An assumption-driven estimate, not a measured saving. Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary AI_COST_SAVED (dictionary).

**`ai.shareTrend`** — Title: AI-touched share of delivered words. Summary: Monthly share of delivered words produced with MTPE or AI-assisted review. How it is calculated: Words in workflows MTPE or AIR ÷ all delivered words in the month. How to interpret it: Noisy month to month; read the trend by quarter. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary AI_SHARE (dictionary).

**`cd.gap`** — Title: Largest gap (words, 8 weeks). Summary: Shortfall in words for the shortfall pair with the highest load. How it is calculated: Pairs are ranked by load (demand ÷ supply); the card shows max(0, demand − supply) for the first shortfall pair. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Needs confirmation: despite the label, this is the gap of the highest-load pair, which is not necessarily the largest gap in words. Check the table's Gap column. Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: Label may not match the calculation · needs confirmation (unverified).

**`cd.heat`** — Title: Load heatmap. Summary: Demand ÷ supply for every language pair and week. How it is calculated: Cell = demand_words ÷ supply_words for one pair-week. Colour scale from 0.4 to 1.6. How to interpret it: Above 1.0 (orange to red) means demand exceeds supply that week. Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/capacity-demand/page.tsx (code).

**`cd.load`** — Title: Capacity load. Summary: Demand words / supply words over the selected weeks (written work only). What it means: Demand words / supply words over the selected weeks (written work only). Both in words. How it is calculated: Σ demand words ÷ Σ supply words over the first 8 forecast weeks, all language pairs (or the ?lp= pair). How to interpret it: Best inside a target band, not as high or as low as possible. Illustrative demo target: <= 90% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Forecast demand = average of the last 8 actual weeks × seasonality × small weekly growth × random noise; AM, SO, HT, VI, ZH carry a seeded +22% surge in some weeks. Supply = linguist capacity × availability. Basis label: KPI dictionary CAP_LOAD · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`cd.short`** — Title: Pairs with a shortfall. Summary: Language pairs whose demand exceeds supply over the next 8 forecast weeks. How it is calculated: Count of pairs with demand ÷ supply > 100% over the first 8 forecast weeks. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Uses a 100% threshold. KPI dictionary CONSTRAINED_LP counts pairs above 90% (shown as Tight in the table). Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/capacity-demand/page.tsx (code).

**`cd.table`** — Title: Capacity load. Summary: Demand, supply, load and gap per language pair over the first 8 forecast weeks. What it means: Demand words / supply words over the selected weeks (written work only). Both in words. How it is calculated: Load = Σ demand ÷ Σ supply; gap = max(0, demand − supply). Status: Shortfall above 100%, Tight above 90%, otherwise OK. How to interpret it: Best inside a target band, not as high or as low as possible. Illustrative demo target: <= 90% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary CAP_LOAD · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`cd.weekly`** — Title: Weekly demand vs supply. Summary: Demand (bars; faded = forecast) against linguist supply (line), in words. How it is calculated: Actual weeks: demand = words in batches that started that week. Forecast demand = average of the last 8 actual weeks × seasonality × small weekly growth × random noise; AM, SO, HT, VI, ZH carry a seeded +22% surge in some weeks.
