Supply = linguist capacity × availability. Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Actual demand is lumpy; forecast weeks are smoothed. An illustrative scenario, not a statistical forecast. Uses a fixed 26-week window (13 actual weeks to 21 Sep 2026, then 13 forecast weeks from 28 Sep 2026); ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/capacity-demand/page.tsx and scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py (code).

**`cd.weeks`** — Title: Forecast weeks. Summary: Number of weekly forecast periods after the data cut-off. How it is calculated: Count of distinct weeks flagged is_forecast. Data source: fact_capacity_period (synthetic demo data). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/capacity-demand/page.tsx (code).

**`cr.health`** — Title: Client health score. Summary: Number of clients in each health band at the 2026-09 quarter-end snapshot. What it means: Composite 0..1: 0.30 OTD(90d) + 0.25 quality(norm) + 0.20 payment timeliness + 0.25 revenue trend (weights renormalised for missing components). Bands: healthy >= 0.70, watch >= 0.50, else at risk. How it is calculated: Health = 0.30 on-time delivery (90 days) + 0.25 quality (normalised) + 0.20 payment timeliness + 0.25 revenue trend; weights are renormalised when a component has no data. Bands: healthy ≥ 0.7, watch ≥ 0.5, otherwise at risk. Bars count clients per band. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 0.70 (not a real company target). Data source: fact_client_period_snapshot (synthetic demo data); calculated in app/(app)/client-revenue/page.tsx. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. This chart counts all clients and is not filtered by business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary HEALTH · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`cr.retention`** — Title: Gross revenue churn. Summary: Gross revenue churn, logo retention and cohort size for the net revenue retention cohort. What it means: Revenue-based gross churn for the NRR cohort: revenue lost from churn and contraction, ignoring expansion. How it is calculated: Cohort = clients with revenue in the opening 12 months (2024-10 to 2025-09). Gross revenue churn = Σ max(0, opening − latest) ÷ Σ opening (expansion ignored). Logo retention = 1 − share of cohort clients with no revenue in the latest 12 months (2025-10 to 2026-09). How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 8% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in nrr() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. The business-unit filter narrows the cohort. Basis label: KPI dictionary GROSS_REV_CHURN / LOGO_RETENTION · window fixed at the cut-off, not the range end (mismatch).

**`cr.roster`** — Title: Client roster. Summary: Every client in scope with period revenue, health score and status. How it is calculated: Revenue = recognised revenue in the selected period. Health and band = 2026-09 snapshot. Status = Churned when the client has a churn date, otherwise Active. Data source: dim_client, fact_revenue_line, fact_client_period_snapshot (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Revenue column uses the selected currency. Optional URL filters: ?tier= and ?health=. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/client-revenue/page.tsx (code).

**`cr.tier`** — Title: Revenue by tier. Summary: Recognised revenue in the period grouped by the client's tier. How it is calculated: Sum of revenue_usd grouped by dim_client.tier. Data source: fact_revenue_line, dim_client (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/client-revenue/page.tsx (code).

**`cr.top10`** — Title: Top 10 clients by revenue. Summary: The ten clients with the most recognised revenue in the selected period. How it is calculated: Sum of revenue_usd per client for the selected months and business unit; largest ten shown. Data source: fact_revenue_line, dim_client (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Client names are fictional. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/client-revenue/page.tsx (code).

**`cr.vertical`** — Title: Revenue by vertical. Summary: Recognised revenue in the period grouped by the client's industry vertical. How it is calculated: Sum of revenue_usd grouped by dim_client.vertical. Data source: fact_revenue_line, dim_client (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/client-revenue/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.checks`** — Title: Schema validation rate. Summary: Passing generator checks / total checks (types, enums, nulls, keys, ranges, reconciliations). How it is calculated: passed checks / total checks Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: No checks -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: 100% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_data_quality_check (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary SCHEMA_VALID · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`dg.dict`** — Title: KPI dictionary. Summary: The single written definition of each KPI, used by the app and the independent Python test reference. Data source: dim_kpi_definition (from scripts/kpi_catalog.py); full detail in docs/kpi-definitions.md. Caveats: ?dom= filters by domain. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.dims`** — Title: Validation pass rate by dimension. Summary: Share of generator checks passed, by quality dimension. How it is calculated: Passed checks ÷ checks for completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, integrity and reconciliation. Data source: fact_data_quality_check (checks run by the data generator; see scripts/validate.py). Basis label: KPI dictionary SCHEMA_VALID, by dimension (dictionary).

**`dg.inventory`** — Title: Table inventory. Summary: Each CSV table with kind, row count, size and SHA-256 prefix, as loaded. Data source: public/data/*.csv (computed by the loader on each load). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.kpis`** — Title: KPI definitions. Summary: Number of KPIs defined in the KPI dictionary. How it is calculated: Count of rows in dim_kpi_definition. Data source: dim_kpi_definition, generated from scripts/kpi_catalog.py. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.prov`** — Title: Dataset provenance. Summary: Version, seed, data window and FX basis of the dataset behind every number. Data source: public/data/meta_dataset.csv. Caveats: Regenerating with the same seed reproduces identical files (verified by test). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.rows`** — Title: Rows (all tables). Summary: Total valid rows across all data tables. How it is calculated: Σ rows loaded from each CSV after validation. Data source: public/data/*.csv (loader report). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.size`** — Title: Dataset size. Summary: Total size of the data CSV files. How it is calculated: Σ file bytes ÷ 1,048,576 (MB), metadata files excluded. Data source: public/data/*.csv (loader report). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`dg.tables`** — Title: Tables. Summary: Number of data files in the generated dataset. How it is calculated: Count of data tables defined in meta_tables.csv and loaded from CSV (dimensions, facts and bridges). Data source: public/data/meta_tables.csv and the loader report. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/data-governance/page.tsx (code).

**`ex.actualPlan`** — Title: Monthly revenue: actual vs plan. Summary: Actual recognised revenue (bars) against the illustrative monthly plan (line). How it is calculated: Actual = monthly recognised revenue. Plan = centred 5-month rolling average of actual monthly revenue × 1.03, scaled by the business unit's revenue share when one is selected. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_kpi_target_period (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Because the plan is derived from actuals, small gaps are expected by construction. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/executive-strategy/page.tsx and scripts/assemble.py (build_targets) (code).

**`ex.okrOnTrack`** — Title: OKRs on track or complete. Summary: Share of the 14 key results whose status is ON_TRACK or COMPLETE. How it is calculated: Count of key results with status ON_TRACK or COMPLETE ÷ all key results. Progress = (current − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline), capped to 0–100%. Status (set by the generator): COMPLETE at 100% progress, ON_TRACK ≥ 70%, AT_RISK ≥ 40%, otherwise OFF_TRACK. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_okr (synthetic demo data); status rule in scripts/assemble.py (build_okrs). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit. This is a count of statuses. KPI dictionary OKR_ATTAIN (mean progress) is a different measure and is shown in the OKR progress chart. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/executive-strategy/page.tsx and scripts/assemble.py (code).

**`ex.okrPillar`** — Title: OKR progress by pillar. Summary: Average key-result progress for each strategic pillar. How it is calculated: Mean of progress over the key results in each pillar; progress = (current − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline), capped to 0–100%. How to interpret it: Higher is better; 100% means every key result in the pillar has reached its target. Data source: fact_okr (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit. Basis label: Matches KPI dictionary OKR_ATTAIN, averaged per pillar (dictionary).

**`ex.okrTable`** — Title: Objectives and key results. Summary: Each key result with its baseline, current value, target, progress and status. How it is calculated: Baseline = same period of the prior year or opening value; progress = (current − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline), capped to 0–100%. Status: COMPLETE at 100%, ON_TRACK ≥ 70%, AT_RISK ≥ 40%, otherwise OFF_TRACK. Data source: fact_okr (synthetic demo data); scripts/assemble.py (build_okrs). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit. Money values are USD; ratios are shown as decimals (0.42 = 42%). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from scripts/assemble.py (build_okrs) (code).

**`ex.revVsPlan`** — Title: Revenue vs plan. Summary: Recognised revenue as a percentage of the illustrative plan for the same months. How it is calculated: Attainment = REV ÷ sum of monthly REV plan targets in the period. With a business unit selected, the plan is scaled by that unit's share of company revenue in the period. How to interpret it: 100% = exactly on plan; above 100% = ahead of plan. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_kpi_target_period (synthetic demo data); app/(app)/executive-strategy/page.tsx. Caveats: The plan is generated from the actuals themselves: a centred 5-month rolling average of monthly revenue × 1.03 (scripts/assemble.py). It is illustrative, not a real budget. KPI dictionary REV_VS_PLAN defines a variance (REV − plan) and shows N/A when a business unit is selected; this card shows actual ÷ plan and scales the plan instead. Basis label: Differs from KPI dictionary REV_VS_PLAN (see caveats) (mismatch).

**`ex.scorecard`** — Title: KPI scorecard. Summary: Six headline KPIs against their illustrative targets for the selected period. How it is calculated: Attainment = actual ÷ target. Revenue target = sum of monthly plan values; other targets = mean of the monthly targets (gross margin 40%, EBITDA margin 13%, on-time delivery 95%, on-demand fill rate 95%, quality score 92). Status: On target ≥ 100% of target, Near ≥ 97%, otherwise Behind. Data source: fact_kpi_target_period and the KPI layer (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Targets are illustrative demo values, not company targets. The dictionary lists slightly different illustrative targets for some KPIs (for example gross margin ≥ 38%); this table uses fact_kpi_target_period. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/executive-strategy/page.tsx and scripts/assemble.py (build_targets) (code).

**`fi.aging`** — Title: Accounts receivable aging. Summary: Open invoice balances grouped by days past due at the cut-off. How it is calculated: Open balance = invoice amount − cash allocated from payments received by 30 Sep 2026; balances of $1 or less are excluded. Buckets by days past due date: not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+. How to interpret it: More value in the older buckets means slower collection and higher credit risk. Data source: fact_invoice_line, bridge_payment_invoice, fact_payment (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/finance-profitability/page.tsx (code).

**`fi.arClient`** — Title: Open receivables by client. Summary: Open and overdue invoice balances per client at the cut-off. How it is calculated: Open = invoiced − cash allocated by 30 Sep 2026 (balances over $1). Overdue = open amount on invoices with a due date before 30 Sep 2026. Data source: fact_invoice_line, bridge_payment_invoice, fact_payment (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/finance-profitability/page.tsx (code).

**`fi.bySl`** — Title: Margin by service line. Summary: Revenue, direct cost and gross margin for each service line in the period. How it is calculated: Gross margin = (revenue − direct cost) ÷ revenue for each service line. Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/finance-profitability/page.tsx (code).

**`fi.margin`** — Title: Margin trend. Summary: Gross margin and EBITDA margin for each month. How it is calculated: Gross margin = (revenue − direct costs) ÷ revenue. EBITDA margin = (gross profit − OPEX) ÷ revenue. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (synthetic demo data); monthlySeries(). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. With a business unit selected, company operating expenses are allocated to it in proportion to its share of revenue. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary GM and EBITDA_M (dictionary).

**`fi.pnl`** — Title: Profit and loss bridge. Summary: From revenue to EBITDA for the period, with each cost category and its share of revenue. How it is calculated: Direct costs: vendor linguists, interpreter pay, MT/AI tooling, platform/telecom, PM and dispatch labour. OPEX: sales and marketing, technology and product, general and admin. Gross profit = revenue − direct costs; EBITDA = gross profit − OPEX. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (synthetic demo data). Caveats: With a business unit selected, company operating expenses are allocated to it in proportion to its share of revenue. Depreciation, amortisation, interest and tax are out of scope. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Matches KPI dictionary DIRECT_COST, GP, OPEX, EBITDA (dictionary).

**`hr.active`** — Title: Active synthetic talent pool. Summary: Resources with is_active = true at the range end. How it is calculated: COUNT(resources active) Unit: Count. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary TALENT_POOL · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`hr.onboard`** — Title: Onboarding time. Summary: Average days from application to onboarded for resources onboarded in the trailing 12 months. How it is calculated: Mean of (onboarded_date − application_date) in days over all resources with an onboarded date. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 30 (not a real company target). Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Not limited to the trailing 12 months as the dictionary describes, and not affected by the reporting period. Not filtered by business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary ONBOARD_DAYS · app averages all onboarded resources (mismatch).

**`hr.pm`** — Title: Project manager workload. Summary: Allocated versus available hours for each project manager in the period. How it is calculated: Allocated = project PM hours spread evenly from start to due date, counted for days inside the period. Capacity = weekly capacity hours × days employed in the period ÷ 7. Utilisation = allocated ÷ capacity. How to interpret it: Above 90% signals overload. Data source: fact_project, dim_owner (synthetic demo data). Caveats: The window ends on the 28th of the last month, so totals differ slightly from the PM utilisation card. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/hr-workforce/page.tsx (code).

**`hr.pmUtil`** — Title: PM utilization. Summary: Estimated PM hours of projects active in the range (spread evenly between start and due) divided by PM available hours (weekly capacity x weeks). How it is calculated: SUM(est_pm_hours allocated to range) / SUM(weekly_capacity_hours x weeks) Numerator: Allocated PM hours. Denominator: PM available hours. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Capacity 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Best inside a target band, not as high or as low as possible. Illustrative demo target: 70-90% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_project, dim_owner (synthetic demo data); calculated in pmUtil() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: The card colours a fall as favourable, but the dictionary treats utilisation as a target band (70–90%). Not filtered by business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary PM_UTIL · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`hr.quality`** — Title: Average quality score (active resources). Summary: Mean of the illustrative quality attribute held on each active linguist and interpreter record. How it is calculated: Mean of dim_resource.quality_score over active resources. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data). Caveats: This is a generated attribute (normal distribution around 93 for internal and 91 for freelance resources), not an average of quality evaluations. Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/hr-workforce/page.tsx and scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py (code).

**`hr.roster`** — Title: Resource roster. Summary: All linguists and interpreters with anonymised codes and fictional attributes. Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data). Caveats: No personal data. Rates are in USD per word or per minute. ?rt= filters by resource type. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/hr-workforce/page.tsx (code).

**`hr.scatter`** — Title: Quality score vs availability. Summary: Each dot is an active resource: illustrative quality score against typical availability. How it is calculated: x = availability (share of capacity typically free); y = quality_score. Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Both are generated attributes; linguist availability is derived from the supply each language pair needs; interpreter availability is random between 30% and 80%. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/hr-workforce/page.tsx and scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py (code).

**`hr.types`** — Title: Active resources by type. Summary: Active linguists and interpreters, internal and freelance. How it is calculated: Count of active resources grouped by resource_type. Data source: dim_resource (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/hr-workforce/page.tsx (code).

**`in.byPair`** — Title: Language-pair performance. Summary: Requests, fulfilled minutes, fill rate and OPI speed to answer per language pair. How it is calculated: Fill rate = fulfilled ÷ (fulfilled + unfulfilled), all request types; cancellations and technical failures excluded. OPI ASA = mean connect_seconds of fulfilled on-demand OPI sessions. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data). Caveats: This fill rate covers scheduled and on-demand requests, unlike the On-demand fill rate card. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/interpretation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`in.hour`** — Title: Requests by hour of day. Summary: All interpretation requests in the period by hour requested. How it is calculated: Count of sessions (any status) by request_hour, 0–23. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Hours are synthetic local time. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/interpretation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`in.modality`** — Title: Fulfilled minutes by modality. Summary: Minutes of fulfilled sessions each month for phone (OPI), video (VRI) and on-site interpreting. How it is calculated: Sum of duration_min for sessions with status FULFILLED, by month and service line. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. The ?mod= URL filter limits it to one modality. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary INT_MIN (dictionary).

**`in.recent`** — Title: Recent sessions. Summary: Up to 1,000 sessions from the selected period, newest first. How it is calculated: The last 1,000 matching rows; the dataset is stored in request-date order, so reversing them shows the newest first. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Search and CSV export apply only to these 1,000 rows. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/interpretation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`ov.alerts`** — Title: Open alerts (top 8). Summary: The eight most severe alerts that are not resolved, with the rule-based exposure estimate. How it is calculated: Alerts with status OPEN or IN_PROGRESS, in the dataset's order: severity (critical first), then exposure, largest first. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data), produced by documented rules in scripts/assemble.py. Caveats: Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Exposure is always in USD and is indicative only. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/overview/page.tsx (code).

**`ov.bySl`** — Title: Revenue by service line. Summary: Recognised revenue in the selected period split by the six service lines. What it means: Service lines (translation, localization, alternative formats, OPI, VRI, on-site) are mutually exclusive revenue categories. Workflows such as MTPE are not service lines, so nothing is double counted. How it is calculated: Sum of revenue_usd grouped by service_line_id, for the selected months and business unit. Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); revBy() in lib/kpi/agg.ts. Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/overview/page.tsx (code).

**`ov.revEbitda`** — Title: Revenue and EBITDA by month. Summary: Monthly recognised revenue (bars) and EBITDA (line). How it is calculated: Revenue = sum of revenue_usd on revenue lines in the month. EBITDA = revenue − direct costs − operating expenses (OPEX allocated by revenue share when a business unit is selected). How to interpret it: Bars show scale and seasonality; the line shows how much of each month's revenue is left after all operating costs. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (synthetic demo data); monthlySeries() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from monthlySeries() in lib/kpi/core.ts (code).

**`qc.ca`** — Title: Open corrective actions. Summary: Evaluations in the period with a corrective action that is still open. How it is calculated: Count of evaluations with corrective_status OPEN and corrective_action other than NONE_REQUIRED. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/quality-compliance/page.tsx (code).

**`qc.errors`** — Title: Errors by category and severity. Summary: Errors logged in the period's evaluations by category, stacked by severity. How it is calculated: Count of error records by category and severity. Weights in the score: minor 1, major 5, critical 25 points per 1,000 words. Pass = score ≥ 90 and no critical errors. Data source: fact_quality_error, fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Illustrative MQM-style framework, not an official certification. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/quality-compliance/page.tsx (code).

**`qc.monthly`** — Title: Average quality score by month. Summary: Mean evaluation score each month on the illustrative 0–100 scale. How it is calculated: Mean of score per month; score = max(0, 100 − (minor × 1 + major × 5 + critical × 25) × 1,000 ÷ sampled words). Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Axis starts at 85 to show variation. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary QUALITY_SCORE (dictionary).

**`qc.perK`** — Title: Errors per 1,000 words. Summary: Logged errors per 1,000 sampled words across evaluations in the period. How it is calculated: (critical + major + minor error counts) ÷ sampled words × 1,000. Counts are not severity-weighted (the quality score applies the weights). How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/quality-compliance/page.tsx (code).

**`qc.table`** — Title: Evaluations. Summary: The 500 most recent evaluations in the period, with error counts, outcome, disputes and corrective actions. Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Linguists appear only as anonymised codes. ?dsev=OPEN shows only open disputes. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/quality-compliance/page.tsx (code).

**`ra.crit`** — Title: Critical + high alerts. Summary: Open alerts with severity CRITICAL or HIGH. How it is calculated: Count of open alerts with severity CRITICAL or HIGH. Severity is set by each rule (for example, an overdue batch worth over $1,500 is CRITICAL). How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data); scripts/assemble.py (build_alerts). Caveats: Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/risk-alerts/page.tsx and scripts/assemble.py (code).

**`ra.domain`** — Title: Open alerts by domain and severity. Summary: Open alerts counted by business domain, stacked by severity. How it is calculated: Rules: R-SLA (overdue or at-risk batches), R-HEALTH (clients at risk), R-CAP (8-week capacity load above 90%), R-DISP (open disputes), R-CA (corrective actions open over 45 days), R-FX (EUR/GBP receivables), R-AR60 (receivables over 60 days past due), R-CONN (7-day connector uptime). Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/risk-alerts/page.tsx and scripts/assemble.py (code).

**`ra.exposure`** — Title: Exposure (USD, indicative). Summary: Sum of the rule-based exposure estimates on open alerts. How it is calculated: Σ exposure_usd over open alerts. Each rule estimates exposure differently: batch revenue (R-SLA), client TTM revenue (R-HEALTH), shortfall words × revenue per word (R-CAP), batch revenue (R-DISP), overdue amount (R-AR60), 10% of foreign-currency receivables (R-FX); R-CA and R-CONN carry no exposure. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data); scripts/assemble.py (build_alerts). Caveats: Exposures overlap and are not additive across rules; indicative only. Always USD; the currency selector does not apply. Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from scripts/assemble.py (build_alerts) (code).

**`ra.matrix`** — Title: Risk matrix. Summary: Open alerts placed by likelihood (rows) and impact (columns) on a 1–5 scale. How it is calculated: Cell = number of open alerts with that likelihood and impact. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Likelihood and impact are drawn at random within a band set by severity (for example CRITICAL: likelihood 4–5). They are illustrative, not assessed scores. Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from scripts/assemble.py (build_alerts) (code).

**`ra.open`** — Title: Open synthetic alerts. Summary: Alerts in state OPEN or IN_PROGRESS (after local acknowledge/dismiss in the browser, which is not persisted). How it is calculated: Count of alerts with status OPEN or IN_PROGRESS. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data); calculated in app/(app)/risk-alerts/page.tsx. Caveats: Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Acknowledging an alert in the table below is local to your browser tab and does not change this count. Basis label: KPI dictionary ALERTS_OPEN · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`ra.resolved`** — Title: Resolved alerts. Summary: Alerts marked RESOLVED in the dataset. How it is calculated: All alerts − open alerts. Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/risk-alerts/page.tsx (code).

**`ra.table`** — Title: Alert list. Summary: Every alert with severity, rule, exposure, owner and recommended action. Select a row to see the rule that raised it. How it is calculated: Rules: R-SLA (overdue or at-risk batches), R-HEALTH (clients at risk), R-CAP (8-week capacity load above 90%), R-DISP (open disputes), R-CA (corrective actions open over 45 days), R-FX (EUR/GBP receivables), R-AR60 (receivables over 60 days past due), R-CONN (7-day connector uptime). Data source: fact_risk_alert (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Acknowledgements are kept in this browser tab only and are lost on refresh. Not filtered by reporting period or business unit. Alert status (open, in progress, resolved) is assigned at random by the generator for demonstration. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from scripts/assemble.py (build_alerts) (code).

**`sc.ai`** — Title: Scenario AI-touched word share. Summary: AI-touched share of written words after the AI adoption change. How it is calculated: a = baseline AI share + AI adoption change, clamped to 0–100%. Baseline share = MTPE + AIR words ÷ all written words on trailing-12-month revenue lines. Data source: lib/scenario.ts and scenarioBaseline() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: The baseline is from revenue lines, so it can differ slightly from the AI-touched share on the AI tab, which uses delivered batches. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from lib/scenario.ts (code).

**`sc.bars`** — Title: Baseline vs scenario. Summary: Revenue, direct costs, gross profit, OPEX and EBITDA for the baseline and the current scenario. How it is calculated: Both bars come from the SCN-F1.0 formulas; the baseline uses all drivers at zero. Data source: lib/scenario.ts. Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from lib/scenario.ts (code).

**`sc.drivers`** — Title: Scenario drivers. Summary: Four what-if inputs applied to the trailing-12-month baseline. How it is calculated: AI adoption change: added to the baseline AI-touched share (clamped to 0–100%); AI words cost less vendor time but add tooling cost. Price change: revenue × (1 + price). Vendor cost inflation: applied to vendor linguist cost and interpreter pay. Volume growth: scales words and revenue; PM labour moves at 0.6× and OPEX at 0.25× of volume. Presets (fact_scenario_assumption_set.csv): Conservative = +3 pp AI, −2% price, +8% vendor cost, −5% volume. Optimistic = +15 pp AI, +3% price, +2% vendor cost, +12% volume. Data source: lib/scenario.ts (formula version SCN-F1.0); presets in fact_scenario_assumption_set.csv; elasticities in meta_config.csv. Caveats: Runs in the browser only; nothing is saved. Illustrative scenario ranges, not statistical forecasts. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from lib/scenario.ts (code).

**`sc.ebitda`** — Title: Scenario EBITDA impact. Summary: Scenario EBITDA less baseline EBITDA; OPEX is semi-fixed (elasticity 0.25 to volume). How it is calculated: EBITDA′ = gross profit′ − OPEX × (1 + 0.25 × volume growth). The card shows EBITDA′ and its difference from the baseline. Baseline = trailing 12 months to 2026-09, all business units. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Comparison basis: Difference from the baseline preset, which reproduces trailing-12-month EBITDA exactly. Data source: Baseline TTM aggregates (synthetic demo data); calculated in lib/scenario.ts (SCN-F1.0). Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: KPI dictionary SCN_EBITDA · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sc.em`** — Title: Scenario EBITDA margin. Summary: Scenario EBITDA as a share of scenario revenue. How it is calculated: EBITDA margin′ = EBITDA′ ÷ revenue′. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Comparison basis: Change vs the baseline preset in percentage points. Data source: lib/scenario.ts (SCN-F1.0). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from lib/scenario.ts (code).

**`sc.gap`** — Title: Scenario capacity gap. Summary: Human words required (human-workflow words + AI words x 0.35 effort factor) less available human capacity words over 12 months. What it means: Human words required (human-workflow words + AI words x 0.35 effort factor) less available human capacity words over 12 months. Positive = shortfall. How it is calculated: Required = words′ × ((1 − a) + 0.35 × a): AI words need 35% of human effort. Supply = 52 × average weekly actual linguist supply. Gap = required − supply; positive = shortfall. How to interpret it: Positive means demand exceeds human capacity; negative means spare capacity. Data source: fact_capacity_period, baseline (synthetic demo data); calculated in lib/scenario.ts (SCN-F1.0). Basis label: KPI dictionary SCN_CAPGAP · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sc.gm`** — Title: Scenario gross margin. Summary: Scenario revenue less scenario direct costs (vendor cost re-priced with AI mix and inflation; PM labour semi-variable; platform variable) / scenario revenue. How it is calculated: Gross profit′ = revenue′ − vendor − tooling − interpreter pay − platform − labour, where: vendor = words′ × ((1 − a) × human cost/word + a × AI cost/word) × (1 + inflation); tooling = words′ × a × tooling/word; interpreter pay × (1 + volume) × (1 + inflation); platform × (1 + volume); labour × (1 + 0.6 × volume). a = AI share. Gross margin′ = gross profit′ ÷ revenue′. Baseline = trailing 12 months to 2026-09, all business units. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Comparison basis: Change vs the baseline preset in percentage points. Data source: Baseline TTM aggregates (synthetic demo data); calculated in lib/scenario.ts (SCN-F1.0). Basis label: KPI dictionary SCN_GM · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sc.revenue`** — Title: Scenario revenue. Summary: Baseline TTM revenue x (1 + volume growth) x (1 + price adjustment). What it means: Baseline TTM revenue x (1 + volume growth) x (1 + price adjustment). Transparent formula, versioned SCN-F1.0. How it is calculated: Revenue′ = baseline revenue × (1 + volume growth) × (1 + price change). Baseline = trailing 12 months to 2026-09, all business units. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Comparison basis: Compared with the baseline preset (all drivers at zero). Data source: Baseline TTM aggregates (synthetic demo data); calculated in lib/scenario.ts (SCN-F1.0). Caveats: Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: KPI dictionary SCN_REVENUE · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sc.traj`** — Title: Forecast / scenario range. Summary: Monthly revenue for the next 12 months if the trailing-12-month average grows at 4% (conservative), 11% (target), 20% (aggressive) a year. What it means: Range between conservative and optimistic preset scenarios. These are illustrative scenario ranges, NOT statistically validated confidence intervals. How it is calculated: Month n = average monthly TTM revenue × (1 + annual rate)^(n ÷ 12), for rates 4% (conservative), 11% (target), 20% (aggressive). Data source: fact_scenario_output (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Illustrative ranges from fixed growth rates, not predictions or confidence intervals. Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from forecasting-scenarios/ScenarioClient.tsx (growth rates from meta_config.csv) (code).

**`sm.funnel`** — Title: Conversion funnel. Summary: Of the opportunities created in the period, how many reached each stage. How it is calculated: Distinct opportunities created in the period with a stage event for LEAD, QUALIFIED, PROPOSAL, NEGOTIATION and CLOSED_WON. Data source: fact_opportunity, fact_opportunity_stage_event (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Recent opportunities may still be progressing, so later stages are understated for recent periods. Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx (code).

**`sm.loss`** — Title: Loss reasons. Summary: Opportunities lost in the period, counted by recorded loss reason. How it is calculated: Count of CLOSED_LOST opportunities with a close date in the period, by loss_reason. Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx (code).

**`sm.open`** — Title: Pipeline value (unweighted). Summary: Sum of estimated annual contract value of open opportunities (stage not closed) at range end. How it is calculated: SUM(value_usd) for opportunities open at range end Unit: USD. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_opportunity, fact_opportunity_stage_event (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: KPI dictionary PIPE_UNW · app measures at the cut-off, not the range end (mismatch).

**`sm.quote`** — Title: Quote turnaround. Summary: Average hours from quote request to quote issued. How it is calculated: Mean quote_turnaround_hours for opportunities created in the selected period. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 24 h (not a real company target). Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data); calculated in app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx. Caveats: Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Basis label: KPI dictionary QUOTE_TAT · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sm.source`** — Title: Win rate by lead source. Summary: Win rate of opportunities closed in the period, by lead source. How it is calculated: Won ÷ all closed (won + lost) for each lead source. Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Small groups can swing widely. Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx (code).

**`sm.table`** — Title: Opportunities. Summary: Every opportunity in the dataset with stage, value, probability and dates. Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Not filtered by the reporting period or business unit; use ?stage= to filter. Prospect names are fictional. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx (code).

**`sm.weighted`** — Title: Pipeline value (weighted). Summary: Open pipeline weighted by stage probability. How it is calculated: SUM(value_usd * probability) Unit: USD. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Probabilities are a configured stage table, not a predictive model. Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: KPI dictionary PIPE_W · app measures at the cut-off, not the range end (mismatch).

**`sm.win`** — Title: Win rate (by count). Summary: Closed-won opportunities / (closed-won + closed-lost) closed in the range. How it is calculated: Won ÷ (won + lost) for opportunities with a close date in the selected period. When there are no closed deals: N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 25% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data); calculated in app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx. Caveats: Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Basis label: KPI dictionary WIN_RATE_COUNT · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`sm.won`** — Title: Won value. Summary: Total estimated annual contract value of opportunities won in the period. How it is calculated: Sum of value_usd for opportunities with stage CLOSED_WON and a close date in the selected period. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_opportunity (synthetic demo data). Caveats: value_usd is an estimated annual contract value, not recognised revenue. Not filtered by business unit (opportunities are not linked to the unit filter). Money is shown in the selected currency, converted once from USD totals at fixed illustrative rates. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/sales-marketing/page.tsx (code).

**`te.daily`** — Title: Daily uptime. Summary: Up minutes ÷ monitored minutes across all simulated connectors, per day. Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. Axis starts at 99%. Basis label: Daily view of KPI dictionary CONN_UPTIME (dictionary).

**`te.degraded`** — Title: Degraded connectors. Summary: Simulated connectors whose 90-day uptime is below 99.5%. How it is calculated: Count of connectors with Σ up minutes ÷ Σ monitored minutes < 0.995. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. The R-CONN alert rule uses the last 7 days instead, so the two counts can differ. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/technology-integration/page.tsx (code).

**`te.err`** — Title: Simulated sync error rate. Summary: SIMULATED: errors (4xx + 5xx + timeout) / requests. How it is calculated: SUM(errors) / SUM(requests) Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Requests 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 1% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. Basis label: KPI dictionary SYNC_ERR · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`te.latency`** — Title: Simulated p95 latency. Summary: SIMULATED: request-weighted mean of daily p95 latency. How it is calculated: Simple mean of daily p95_ms across all connector-days. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 400 ms (not a real company target). Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. The dictionary defines a request-weighted mean; the app uses an unweighted mean. Basis label: KPI dictionary LATENCY_P95 · app uses an unweighted mean (mismatch).

**`te.mix`** — Title: Error mix. Summary: Simulated errors over 90 days by type: 4xx client, 5xx server and timeouts. Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/technology-integration/page.tsx (code).

**`te.table`** — Title: Connector health. Summary: Uptime, requests, error rate, records and latency for each simulated connector. How it is calculated: Status: Degraded when 90-day uptime < 0.995, otherwise Healthy. p95 and p99 are simple means of daily values. Data source: dim_connector, fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. Endpoints use the reserved .invalid domain and are never contacted. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/technology-integration/page.tsx (code).

**`te.uptime`** — Title: Simulated connector uptime. Summary: SIMULATED: up minutes / monitored minutes across connectors in the window. What it means: SIMULATED: up minutes / monitored minutes across connectors in the window. Not production uptime. How it is calculated: SUM(up_minutes) / SUM(monitored_minutes) Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Denominator 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 99.5% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_integration_telemetry (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Caveats: Telemetry is SIMULATED: no real systems are connected. Covers all 90 days of telemetry; ignores the reporting period and business unit. Basis label: KPI dictionary CONN_UPTIME · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`tr.active`** — Title: Active batches. Summary: Every batch not yet delivered, with progress and status. How it is calculated: Status uses the same rule as Pipeline status. Data source: fact_translation_batch, dim_client (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/translation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`tr.byPair`** — Title: Performance by language pair. Summary: Delivered batches, words, on-time rate, turnaround and AI-touched share for each language pair. How it is calculated: Delivered batches in the period and business unit, grouped by language pair. On-time = delivered_date ≤ due_date; turnaround = mean days from start to delivery; AI-touched share = non-HT words ÷ all words. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data). Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/translation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`tr.monthly`** — Title: Words delivered and on-time rate by month. Summary: Delivered words (bars) and the share of batches delivered by their due date (line). How it is calculated: Words = sum of words_total for batches delivered in the month. On-time rate = batches with delivered_date ≤ due_date ÷ batches delivered in the month. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Shows all 33 months (2024-01 to 2026-09) regardless of the reporting period; the business-unit filter applies. Basis label: Monthly view of KPI dictionary TR_WORDS and TR_OTD (dictionary).

**`tr.stage`** — Title: Active pipeline by stage. Summary: Batches not yet delivered, counted by current production stage. How it is calculated: Count of batches with status other than DELIVERED, grouped by stage. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/translation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`tr.status`** — Title: Pipeline status. Summary: Active batches classified as on track, at risk or overdue. How it is calculated: Overdue: due date before 30 Sep 2026. At risk: due within 2 days and under 80% complete. Otherwise on track. How to interpret it: Overdue and at-risk batches need re-assignment or a revised delivery date. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); thresholds in the dataset manifest. Caveats: Measured at the data cut-off (30 Sep 2026); the reporting-period selector does not change it. URL filters ?lp= and ?stage= narrow these counts. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/translation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`tr.workflow`** — Title: Workflow mix (words). Summary: Delivered words in the period by workflow: human translation (HT), MT post-editing (MTPE) and AI-assisted review (AIR). How it is calculated: Sum of words_total of delivered batches, grouped by workflow_id. How to interpret it: A larger MTPE + AIR share means more AI-touched work. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Workflow is separate from service line, so MTPE words are not a revenue category and are never double counted. Basis label: Not in the KPI dictionary · derived from app/(app)/translation-ops/page.tsx (code).

**`ACTIVE_CLIENTS`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Active clients. Summary: Clients with recognised revenue > 0 in the selected range. How it is calculated: COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) with revenue_usd > 0 in range Unit: Count. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary ACTIVE_CLIENTS · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`AI_COST_SAVED`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Estimated cost impact. Summary: Estimate: hours saved x blended review hourly cost less tooling cost. How it is calculated: SUM(est_cost_saved_usd) Unit: USD. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary AI_COST_SAVED · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`AI_EDIT_DIST`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Post-edit distance. Summary: Word-weighted mean normalised edit distance on AI-touched batches (0 = unchanged, 1 = rewritten). What it means: Word-weighted mean normalised edit distance on AI-touched batches (0 = unchanged, 1 = rewritten). Distinct from MTQE, BLEU and COMET. How it is calculated: SUM(edit_distance x words) / SUM(words) Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: No batches -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch, fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary AI_EDIT_DIST · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`AI_HOURS_SAVED`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Estimated hours saved. Summary: Estimate: words / baseline human words per hour minus words / observed words per hour. What it means: Estimate: words / baseline human words per hour minus words / observed words per hour. An estimate, not a measured result. How it is calculated: SUM(est_hours_saved) Unit: Hours. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary AI_HOURS_SAVED · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`AI_SHARE`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: AI-touched word share. Summary: Words in AI-touched workflows (MTPE or AIR) divided by delivered written words in the same range and population as TR_WORDS. How it is calculated: SUM(words | workflow in MTPE, AIR) / TR_WORDS Numerator: AI-touched words. Denominator: Delivered words. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: TR_WORDS = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary AI_SHARE · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`ARPA`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Average revenue per account. Summary: Revenue divided by active clients in the same range. How it is calculated: ARPA = REV / ACTIVE_CLIENTS Numerator: REV. Denominator: ACTIVE_CLIENTS. Unit: USD. When there is no data: Active = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary ARPA · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`DSO`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Days sales outstanding (demo formula). Summary: Simplified demo DSO: open receivables at the range end divided by invoiced value in the trailing 90 days, times 90. What it means: Simplified demo DSO: open receivables at the range end divided by invoiced value in the trailing 90 days, times 90. Receivable = invoiced less allocated cash receipts received on or before the range end. How it is calculated: DSO = open_AR_usd(end) / invoiced_usd(end-89d..end) * 90 Numerator: open AR. Denominator: invoiced last 90 days. Unit: Days. When there is no data: Invoiced = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 50 days (not a real company target). Data source: fact_invoice_line, bridge_payment_invoice, fact_payment (synthetic demo data); calculated in dso() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary DSO · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`EBITDA`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: EBITDA. Summary: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation = gross profit less operating expenses. What it means: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation = gross profit less operating expenses. D&A is shown separately below EBITDA in the bridge; interest and tax are out of scope. How it is calculated: EBITDA = GP - OPEX Unit: USD. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_cost_line, fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary EBITDA · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`EBITDA_M`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: EBITDA margin. Summary: EBITDA / recognised revenue. How it is calculated: EBITDA_M = EBITDA / REV Numerator: EBITDA. Denominator: REV. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: REV = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 12% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_cost_line, fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary EBITDA_M · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`FILL_ON_DEMAND`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: On-demand fill rate. Summary: Fulfilled on-demand OPI/VRI requests divided by on-demand requests excluding client cancellations and VRI technical failures. How it is calculated: FULFILLED / (FULFILLED + UNFULFILLED) for ON_DEMAND Numerator: Fulfilled on-demand. Denominator: Fulfilled + unfulfilled on-demand. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Denominator 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 95% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary FILL_ON_DEMAND · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`GM`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Gross margin. Summary: Gross profit as a share of the same-basis recognised revenue. How it is calculated: GM = GP / REV Numerator: GP. Denominator: REV. Unit: Fraction (shown %). When there is no data: REV = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 38% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary GM · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`GP`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Gross profit. Summary: Recognised revenue less direct costs (categories listed in DIRECT_COST). What it means: Recognised revenue less direct costs (categories listed in DIRECT_COST). Operating expenses and D&A are excluded. How it is calculated: GP = REV - DIRECT_COST Unit: USD. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_revenue_line, fact_cost_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary GP · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`INT_AVG_DUR`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Average session duration. Summary: Mean duration of fulfilled sessions. How it is calculated: AVG(duration_min | FULFILLED) Unit: Minutes. When there is no data: No sessions -> N/A. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary INT_AVG_DUR · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`INT_MIN`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Interpretation minutes delivered. Summary: Minutes of FULFILLED sessions in the range (scheduled demand and cancellations excluded). How it is calculated: SUM(duration_min) where status = FULFILLED Unit: Minutes. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary INT_MIN · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`MTQE_ACCEPT`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: MTQE acceptance. Summary: Words whose segment-level quality-estimation score met the acceptance threshold (default 0.85) divided by AI-touched words in the same population. How it is calculated: SUM(mtqe_accepted_words) / SUM(AI words) Numerator: Accepted words. Denominator: AI words. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: No batches -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_ai_workflow_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary MTQE_ACCEPT · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`NRR`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Net revenue retention. Summary: Fixed opening cohort = clients with revenue in the 12 months ending 12 months before the range end. What it means: Fixed opening cohort = clients with revenue in the 12 months ending 12 months before the range end. NRR = cohort revenue in the latest 12 months / cohort revenue in the opening 12 months. New clients are excluded; expansion and contraction included. How it is calculated: NRR = SUM(cohort revenue, latest 12m) / SUM(cohort revenue, opening 12m) Numerator: Cohort latest-12m revenue. Denominator: Cohort opening-12m revenue. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Opening = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 100% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in nrr() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary NRR · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`OPEN_DISPUTES`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Open disputes. Summary: Evaluations with dispute_status = OPEN. How it is calculated: COUNT(dispute_status = OPEN) Unit: Count. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary OPEN_DISPUTES · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`OPI_ASA`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: OPI average speed to answer. Summary: Mean seconds to connect for FULFILLED on-demand OPI sessions. What it means: Mean seconds to connect for FULFILLED on-demand OPI sessions. Applies to OPI only. How it is calculated: AVG(connect_seconds | OPI, ON_DEMAND, FULFILLED) Unit: Seconds. When there is no data: No sessions -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 30 s (not a real company target). Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary OPI_ASA · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`QUALITY_SCORE`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Quality score. Summary: Mean evaluation score on the single illustrative 0-100 framework (ILLUSTRATIVE_MQM_STYLE): 100 minus weighted error penalties per 1,000 sampled words (minor 1, major 5, critical 25). How it is calculated: AVG(score) Unit: Score 0-100. When there is no data: No evaluations -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 92 (not a real company target). Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary QUALITY_SCORE · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`REJECTION_RATE`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Client rejection rate. Summary: Delivered batches rejected by the client divided by delivered batches in the range. How it is calculated: SUM(client_rejected) / delivered batches Numerator: Rejected batches. Denominator: Delivered batches. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: No batches -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 3% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary REJECTION_RATE · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`REV`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Recognized revenue. Summary: Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. What it means: Revenue recognised in the period: written work when a batch is delivered, interpretation when fulfilled minutes are served. Not bookings, invoices or cash. How it is calculated: SUM(revenue_usd) over revenue lines in range, converted to reporting currency Unit: USD (or EUR/GBP). When there is no data: Empty set = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: Plan = smoothed trend +3% (fact_kpi_target_period) (not a real company target). Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary REV · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`REVIEW_PASS`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Review pass rate. Summary: Evaluations with outcome PASS divided by all evaluations. How it is calculated: PASS / evaluations Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: None -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 90% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_quality_evaluation (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary REVIEW_PASS · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`TM_REUSE`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Translation-memory reuse. Summary: Words covered by TM matches divided by delivered words in the same population. How it is calculated: SUM(tm_match_words) / TR_WORDS Numerator: TM-matched words. Denominator: Delivered words. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: TR_WORDS = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary TM_REUSE · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`TOP10_CONC`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Top-10 client concentration. Summary: Share of revenue from the ten largest clients in the range. How it is calculated: SUM(revenue of top 10 clients) / REV Numerator: Top-10 revenue. Denominator: REV. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: REV = 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Illustrative demo target: <= 55% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_revenue_line (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary TOP10_CONC · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`TR_OTD`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Translation on-time delivery. Summary: Delivered batches with delivered_date <= due_date divided by all delivered batches in the range. How it is calculated: on_time_batches / delivered_batches Numerator: On-time batches. Denominator: Delivered batches. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: No batches -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 95% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary TR_OTD · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`TR_TAT`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Average turnaround time. Summary: Mean calendar days from batch start to delivery for delivered batches. How it is calculated: AVG(delivered_date - start_date) Unit: Days. When there is no data: No batches -> N/A. How to interpret it: Lower is better. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary TR_TAT · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`TR_WORDS`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: Translation words delivered. Summary: Words in batches with status DELIVERED and delivered_date in the range (eligible population: all written batches). How it is calculated: SUM(words_total) for delivered batches Unit: Words. When there is no data: Empty = 0. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Data source: fact_translation_batch (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary TR_WORDS · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`VRI_CONN`** (KPI dictionary) — Title: VRI connection success. Summary: VRI sessions that connected divided by VRI sessions where an interpreter was assigned (FULFILLED + TECH_FAILURE). What it means: VRI sessions that connected divided by VRI sessions where an interpreter was assigned (FULFILLED + TECH_FAILURE). Applies to VRI only. How it is calculated: FULFILLED / (FULFILLED + TECH_FAILURE) for VRI Numerator: VRI fulfilled. Denominator: VRI fulfilled + tech failure. Unit: Fraction. When there is no data: Denominator 0 -> N/A. How to interpret it: Higher is better. Illustrative demo target: >= 97% (not a real company target). Data source: fact_interpretation_session (synthetic demo data); calculated in core() in lib/kpi/core.ts. Basis label: KPI dictionary VRI_CONN · matches the app calculation (dictionary).

**`PERIOD_INFO`** (header) — Title: Reporting period. Summary: Chooses the whole calendar months that KPIs, charts and tables on most tabs are calculated over. How it is calculated: Year to date: 2026-01 to 2026-09. Quarter to date and Last 3 months: the latest 3 months (2026-07 to 2026-09). Trailing 12 months: 2025-10 to 2026-09. Last 6 months: 2026-04 to 2026-09. Latest month: 2026-09. All data: 2024-01 to 2026-09 (33 months). Custom: any span of whole months between 2024-01 and 2026-09. Comparison basis: KPI cards that show a change compare with the prior period: the same months of 2025 for Year to date, otherwise the equal-length window just before the selection. There is no comparison for All data, or when that window would start before 2024-01. Data source: lib/filters.ts (windowMonths, priorMonths). Synthetic demo data ends at the 30 Sep 2026 cut-off. Caveats: Ranges are whole months, not days, so every figure reconciles to monthly revenue and cost. Ignored by: Capacity & Demand (fixed 26-week window), Technology & Integration (fixed 90 days), Risk & Alerts, Data Governance, and Forecasting & Scenarios (always the trailing 12 months). Always measured at the cut-off regardless of range: net revenue retention, DSO, open pipeline, active resources, client health bands and the active translation pipeline.

**`BU_INFO`** (header) — Title: Business unit. Summary: Limits client-based figures to clients assigned to the selected synthetic unit (Alpha, Beta or Gamma). How it is calculated: Revenue lines, translation batches, interpretation sessions, quality evaluations and receivables are kept when their client's business unit matches. Operating expenses are company-level; with a unit selected they are allocated to it in proportion to its share of revenue, so EBITDA becomes an allocation. Data source: dim_client.business_unit (synthetic demo data). Caveats: Not applied on Sales & Marketing, HR & Workforce, Capacity & Demand, Technology & Integration, Risk & Alerts, Data Governance or Forecasting & Scenarios. On Client & Revenue, the client health band chart is not filtered by business unit. On Executive Strategy, the revenue plan is scaled by the unit's share of revenue, because plans exist only at company level.

**`RESET_INFO`** (header) — Title: Reset. Summary: Clears every filter in the page URL and returns to Year to date, USD and all business units. Caveats: Also clears page-specific URL filters such as ?tier=, ?lp= or ?stage=.

**`currency`** (header) — Title: Reporting currency. Summary: Changes how money is displayed (USD, EUR or GBP). Underlying amounts are stored in USD. How it is calculated: Displayed amount = USD total ÷ rate, with 1 EUR = 1.08 USD and 1 GBP = 1.27 USD (rate set DEMO-FX-2026-09). Conversion is applied once to aggregated totals and rounded only for display, to avoid rounding drift. Data source: public/data/dim_fx_rate.csv (synthetic demo data), read by fxRate() in lib/data/store.ts. Caveats: Fixed illustrative rates, not market rates; percentages and ratios are unaffected. Some values always stay in USD: alert exposure on Risk & Alerts, money values in the OKR table, and resource rates on HR & Workforce.

**`demo`** (header) — Title: Synthetic demo data. Summary: Every client, linguist, amount and event in this app is fictional and generated for an interview demonstration. How it is calculated: Generated by scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py with fixed seed 20261029; dataset 2026.10.1, window 2024-01 to 2026-09, cut-off 2026-09-30. Data source: public/data/meta_dataset.csv. Caveats: No real company, client or employee data is represented, and no figure is a real result or target. All records are synthetic and fictional. Nothing here is BIG Language Solutions data.
